title.zh: 卷七十六 志第二十七上: 祭祀五
title.raw: 卷七十六 志第二十七上: 祭祀五 Volume 76 Treatises 29: Offerings 5

sentences.zh: 祭祀五 ○太社太稷

translations.literal: Offerings V ○ The Great Altar of Soil and the Great Altar of Grain
translations.idiomatic: Offerings V — The Great Altars of Soil and Grain

sentences.zh: 至元七年十二月，有詔歲祀太社太稷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Zhiyuan, there was an edict that the Great Altars of Soil and Grain should be sacrificed to each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of the Zhiyuan era (1270), an edict ordered annual sacrifices at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，始用御史中丞崔彧言，於和義門內少南，得地四十畝，為壝垣，近南為二壇，壇高五丈，方廣如之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year, they first adopted the proposal of Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu: inside Heyi Gate, slightly to the south, they obtained forty mu of land, built an enclosing rampart, and near the south erected two altars, each five zhang high, square in breadth and length to match.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirtieth year (1293), the court adopted the proposal of Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu. Inside Heyi Gate, a little to the south, they took forty mu of land, raised an enclosing rampart, and near its southern side built two altars five zhang high, each square on every side.

sentences.zh: 社東稷西，相去約五丈。

translations.literal: The Soil altar was east and the Grain altar west, separated by about five zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of Soil stood to the east and the altar of Grain to the west, about five zhang apart.

sentences.zh: 社壇土用青赤白黑四色，依方位築之，中間實以常土，上以黃土覆之。

translations.literal: For the Soil altar, earth of the four colors blue-green, red, white, and black was used, piled according to the cardinal directions; the center was filled with ordinary earth and covered on top with yellow earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Soil altar was built of earth in four colors—blue-green, red, white, and black—laid out by the cardinal directions, with ordinary earth packed in the center and yellow earth spread on top.

sentences.zh: 築必堅實，依方面以五色泥飾之。

translations.literal: The construction had to be solid and firm; on each face it was adorned with colored mud of the five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The mound had to be packed solid, and each face was finished with mud in the corresponding ritual color.

sentences.zh: 四面當中，各設一陛道。

translations.literal: At the center of each of the four sides, one flight of steps was set.
translations.idiomatic: A stairway was placed at the midpoint of each of the four sides.

sentences.zh: 其廣一丈，亦各依方色。

translations.literal: Each was one zhang wide and likewise colored according to its direction.
translations.idiomatic: Each stairway was one zhang wide and painted in the color of its direction.

sentences.zh: 稷壇一如社壇之制，惟土不用五色，其上四周純用一色黃土。

translations.literal: The Grain altar followed the same regulations as the Soil altar, except that its earth did not use the five colors; on top and on all four sides only yellow earth was used throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The Grain altar followed the same design as the Soil altar, except that its earth was not laid in five colors; top and sides alike were built entirely of yellow earth.

sentences.zh: 壇皆北向，立北墉於社壇之北，以磚為之，飾以黃泥；

translations.literal: Both altars faced north. A northern screen wall was erected north of the Soil altar, made of brick and adorned with yellow mud;
translations.idiomatic: Both altars faced north. North of the Soil altar stood a northern screen wall of brick, plastered with yellow mud;

sentences.zh: 瘞坎二於稷壇之北，少西，深足容物。

translations.literal: two burial pits were placed north of the Grain altar, slightly to the west, deep enough to hold the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: two burial pits were dug north of the Grain altar, a little to the west, deep enough to receive the buried offerings.

sentences.zh: 二壇周圍壝垣，以磚為之，高五丈，廣三十丈，四隅連飾。

translations.literal: An enclosing rampart surrounded the two altars, built of brick, five zhang high and thirty zhang wide, with continuous ornamentation at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: A brick enclosing rampart ringed the two altars, five zhang high and thirty zhang across, with the corners finished in a continuous design.

sentences.zh: 內壝垣欞星門四所，外垣欞星門二所，每所門二，列戟二十有四。

translations.literal: On the inner rampart were four Spirit Star gates; on the outer wall, two Spirit Star gates; each site had two doors, with twenty-four halberds arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: The inner rampart had four Spirit Star gates; the outer wall had two, each with paired doors and twenty-four halberds set in rank.

sentences.zh: 外壝內北垣下屋七間，南望二壇，以備風雨，曰望祀堂。

translations.literal: Within the outer rampart, beneath the northern wall, were seven rooms facing south toward the two altars, to shelter from wind and rain, called the Hall for Distant Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the outer rampart, seven rooms stood under the northern wall, facing south toward the altars as shelter from the weather—the Hall for Distant Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 堂東屋五間，連廈三間，曰齊班廳。

translations.literal: East of the hall were five rooms with a connected corridor of three bays, called the Hall for Assembling in Formation.
translations.idiomatic: East of the hall stood five rooms with a three-bay corridor attached, called the Hall for Assembling in Formation.

sentences.zh: 廳之南，西向屋八間，曰獻官幕。

translations.literal: South of the hall, eight rooms facing west were called the Offering Officials' Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: South of that hall, eight rooms facing west served as the Offering Officials' Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又南，西向屋三間，曰院官齋所。

translations.literal: Farther south, three rooms facing west were called the Court Officials' Abstinence Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south, three west-facing rooms were the Court Officials' Abstinence Quarters.

sentences.zh: 又其南，屋十間，自北而南，曰祠祭局，曰儀鸞庫，曰法物庫，曰都監庫，曰雅樂庫。

translations.literal: Still farther south, ten rooms from north to south were named, in order: the Sacrificial Administration, the Ceremonial Insignia Storehouse, the Ritual Objects Storehouse, the Chief Supervisory Storehouse, and the Court Music Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther south, ten rooms ran from north to south: the Sacrificial Administration, the Ceremonial Insignia Storehouse, the Ritual Objects Storehouse, the Chief Supervisory Storehouse, and the Court Music Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 又其南，北向屋三間，曰百官廚。

translations.literal: Still farther south, three rooms facing north were called the Hundred Officials' Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south again, three north-facing rooms were the Hundred Officials' Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 外垣南門西壝垣西南，北向屋三間，曰大樂署。

translations.literal: Southwest of the outer wall's south gate and western rampart, three rooms facing north were called the Grand Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the south gate on the outer wall's western side stood three north-facing rooms, the Grand Music Office.

sentences.zh: 其西，東向屋三間，曰樂工房。

translations.literal: West of it, three rooms facing east were called the Musicians' Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: To its west, three east-facing rooms housed the musicians.

sentences.zh: 又其北，北向屋一間，曰饌幕殿。

translations.literal: Farther north, one room facing north was called the Offering Pavilion Hall.
translations.idiomatic: North of that stood a single north-facing room, the Offering Pavilion Hall.

sentences.zh: 又北，南向屋三間，曰饌幕。

translations.literal: Farther north, three rooms facing south were called the Offering Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther north, three south-facing rooms formed the Offering Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又北稍東，南向門一間。

translations.literal: Farther north and slightly east was one south-facing gate.
translations.idiomatic: A little farther north and slightly east stood a single south-facing gate.

sentences.zh: 院內南，南向屋三間，曰神廚。

translations.literal: Within the compound to the south, three rooms facing south were called the Spirit Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the compound on the south side, three south-facing rooms were the Spirit Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 東向屋三間，曰酒庫。

translations.literal: Three rooms facing east were called the Wine Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Three east-facing rooms served as the Wine Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 近北少卻，東向屋三間，曰犧牲房。

translations.literal: Near the north, set back slightly, three rooms facing east were called the Sacrificial Victims' Room.
translations.idiomatic: A little to the north, set slightly back, three east-facing rooms housed the sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 井有亭。

translations.literal: The well had a pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A pavilion covered the well.

sentences.zh: 望祀堂後自西而東，南向屋九間，曰執事齋郎房。

translations.literal: Behind the Hall for Distant Sacrifice, from west to east, nine rooms facing south were called the Ritual Attendants' and Acolytes' Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the Hall for Distant Sacrifice, nine south-facing rooms ran from west to east—the quarters for ritual attendants and acolytes.

sentences.zh: 自北折而南，西向屋九間，曰監祭執事房。

translations.literal: Turning from the north and bending south, nine rooms facing west were called the Sacrifice Supervisors' and Ritual Attendants' Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Turning south from the north side, nine west-facing rooms were the quarters for sacrifice supervisors and ritual attendants.

sentences.zh: 此壇壝次舍之所也。

translations.literal: These were the lodgings within the altar enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the buildings within the altar precinct.

sentences.zh: 社主用白石，長五尺，廣二尺，剡其上如鐘，於社壇近南，北向，埋其半於土中。

translations.literal: For the Soil lord, white stone was used, five feet long and two feet wide, its top carved like a bell; it was placed near the south of the Soil altar, facing north, with half buried in the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Soil was represented by a white stone five feet long and two feet wide, its upper end carved like a bell. Near the south side of the Soil altar it stood facing north, half buried in the ground.

sentences.zh: 稷不用主。

translations.literal: For Grain, no lord-stone was used.
translations.idiomatic: The altar of Grain had no lord-stone.

sentences.zh: 后土氏配社，後稷氏配稷。

translations.literal: Queen Earth was paired with Soil; Lord Millet was paired with Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Earth was associated with the Soil altar; Lord Millet with the Grain altar.

sentences.zh: 神位版二，用栗，素質黑書。

translations.literal: There were two spirit tablets of chestnut wood, plain in substance with black inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Two spirit tablets of chestnut wood bore plain surfaces with characters written in black.

sentences.zh: 社樹以松，於社稷二壇之南各一株。

translations.literal: For the Soil altar, pine was used as the sacred tree; south of each of the two altars of Soil and Grain, one tree was planted.
translations.idiomatic: Pine served as the sacred tree of Soil; one tree stood south of each of the two altars.

sentences.zh: 此作主樹木之法也。

translations.literal: These were the regulations for the lord-stones and sacred trees.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the rules governing the lord-stones and sacred trees.

sentences.zh: 祝版四，以楸木為之，各長二尺四寸，闊一尺二寸，厚一分。

translations.literal: There were four prayer boards of catalpa wood, each two feet four inches long, one foot two inches wide, and one fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Four prayer boards of catalpa wood measured two feet four inches long, one foot two inches wide, and one fen thick.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「維年月日，嗣天子敬遣某官某，敢昭告於太社之神。」

translations.literal: The text read: "On such-and-such a year, month, and day, the heir Son of Heaven respectfully sends such-and-such an official to declare plainly to the spirit of the Great Altar of Soil."
translations.idiomatic: The text ran: "On [year], [month], [day], the heir Son of Heaven respectfully dispatches [official] to announce plainly to the spirit of the Great Altar of Soil."

sentences.zh: 配位曰后土之神。

translations.literal: The associated seat read: "the spirit of Queen Earth."
translations.idiomatic: The associated seat was inscribed to the spirit of Queen Earth.

sentences.zh: 稷曰太稷之神，配位曰後稷之神。

translations.literal: For Grain it read "the spirit of the Great Altar of Grain"; for the associated seat, "the spirit of Lord Millet."
translations.idiomatic: For Grain: "the spirit of the Great Altar of Grain"; for the associated seat: "the spirit of Lord Millet."

sentences.zh: 玉幣，社稷皆黝圭一，繅藉瘞玉一，以黝石代之，玄幣一。

translations.literal: For jade and silks, Soil and Grain each had one dark jade scepter, one silken wrapping with buried jade (dark stone substituted), and one black silk.
translations.idiomatic: For jade and silks, each altar received one dark jade scepter, one wrapped burial jade (dark stone in place of jade), and one length of black silk.

sentences.zh: 配位皆玄幣一，各長一丈八尺。

translations.literal: Each associated seat had one black silk, each one zhang eight feet long.
translations.idiomatic: Each associated seat had one length of black silk, eighteen feet long.

sentences.zh: 此祝文玉幣之式也。

translations.literal: These were the forms for the prayer text and jade and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the prescribed forms for the prayer text, jade, and silks.

sentences.zh: 牛一，其色黝，其角握，有副。

translations.literal: One ox, dark in color, with horns that could be grasped in the hand, with a secondary victim.
translations.idiomatic: One dark-colored ox with hand-span horns, plus a secondary victim.

sentences.zh: 羊四，野豕四。

translations.literal: Four sheep and four wild boars.
translations.idiomatic: Four sheep and four wild boars.

sentences.zh: 籩之實皆十，無糗餌、粉餈。

translations.literal: The contents of the baskets were ten each, without dried grain cakes or powdered rice cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Each basket held ten offerings, but without dried grain cakes or powdered rice cakes.

sentences.zh: 豆之實亦十，無厓食、糝食。

translations.literal: The contents of the stands were also ten each, without edge-meat or seasoned grain.
translations.idiomatic: Each stand likewise held ten items, but without edge-meat or seasoned grain.

sentences.zh: 簠簋之實皆四，铏之實和羹五，齊皆以尚醞代之。

translations.literal: The grain vessels held four each; the tripods held five harmonized broths; all fermented offerings were replaced with imperial brew.
translations.idiomatic: The grain vessels held four portions each; the tripods held five harmonized broths; all fermented offerings were replaced with imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 香用沈龍涎。

translations.literal: For incense, sinking agarwood and dragon's saliva were used.
translations.idiomatic: Incense consisted of sinking agarwood and ambergris.

sentences.zh: 神席一，緣以黑綾，黑綾褥方七尺四寸。

translations.literal: One spirit mat, bordered with black gauze; a black gauze cushion, square, seven feet four inches.
translations.idiomatic: One spirit mat trimmed with black gauze, with a square black gauze cushion seven feet four inches on a side.

sentences.zh: 太尊、著尊、犧尊、山罍各二，有坫，加勺冪。

translations.literal: Grand, Secondary, Sacrificial, and Mountain wine vessels, two of each, with stands, fitted with ladles and covers.
translations.idiomatic: Two each of the grand, secondary, sacrificial, and mountain wine vessels, each on a stand with ladle and cover.

sentences.zh: 象尊、壺尊、山罍各二，有坫冪，設而不酌。

translations.literal: Elephant, Jar, and Mountain vessels, two of each, with stands and covers, set out but not poured from.
translations.idiomatic: Two each of the elephant, jar, and mountain vessels, on stands with covers, displayed but not poured from.

sentences.zh: 籩豆各十有一，其一設於饌幕。

translations.literal: Baskets and stands, eleven each; one set was placed in the Offering Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven baskets and eleven stands apiece, one set of each kept in the Offering Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 铏三，簠三，簋三，其一設於饌幕。

translations.literal: Three tripods, three grain boxes, and three grain bowls; one set was placed in the Offering Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Three tripods, three grain boxes, and three grain bowls, with one set of each in the Offering Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 俎八，其二設於饌幕。

translations.literal: Eight offering tables; two were set in the Offering Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Eight offering tables, two of them kept in the Offering Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 盤一，毛血豆一，爵一，有坫。

translations.literal: One tray, one stand for hair and blood, one libation cup with a stand.
translations.idiomatic: One tray, one stand for hair and blood, and one libation cup on its stand.

sentences.zh: 沙池一，玉幣篚一，木柶一，勺一，香鼎一，香盒一，香案一，祝案一，皆有衣。

translations.literal: One sand basin, one basket for jade and silks, one wooden spoon, one ladle, one incense tripod, one incense box, one incense table, one prayer table—all with covers.
translations.idiomatic: One sand basin, one basket for jade and silks, one wooden spoon, one ladle, and one each of incense tripod, incense box, incense table, and prayer table, all with draped covers.

sentences.zh: 紅髹器一，以盛馬湩。

translations.literal: One red-lacquered vessel to hold mare's milk.
translations.idiomatic: One red-lacquered vessel for mare's milk.

sentences.zh: 盥洗位二，罍二，洗二。

translations.literal: Two hand-washing stations, two jars, and two basins.
translations.idiomatic: Two hand-washing stations, each with a jar and a basin.

sentences.zh: 白羅巾四，實以篚。

translations.literal: Four white gauze towels, stored in a basket.
translations.idiomatic: Four white gauze towels, kept in a basket.

sentences.zh: 朱漆盤五。

translations.literal: Five vermilion-lacquered trays.
translations.idiomatic: Five vermilion-lacquered trays.

sentences.zh: 已上，社稷皆同。

translations.literal: All of the above were the same for Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above applied alike to both altars.

sentences.zh: 配位有象尊，無太尊。

translations.literal: The associated seats had elephant vessels but no grand vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Associated seats had elephant vessels but not grand vessels.

sentences.zh: 設而不酌者，無象尊。

translations.literal: For those set out but not poured from, there were no elephant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Display vessels not poured from included no elephant vessels.

sentences.zh: 餘皆與正位同。

translations.literal: The rest were the same as for the principal seats.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else matched the principal seats.

sentences.zh: 此牲齊祭器之等也。

translations.literal: These were the grades of victims, fermented offerings, and ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the prescribed victims, fermented offerings, and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 饌幕、省饌殿、香殿，黃羅幕三，黃羅額四，黃絹帷一百九十五幅，獻攝板位三十有五，紫綾拜褥百，蒲、葦席各二百，木燈籠四十，絳羅燈衣百一十，紅挑燈十，剪燭刀二，鐵籸盆三十有架，黃燭二百，雜用燭二百，麻籸三百，松明、清油各百斤。

translations.literal: For the Offering Pavilion, Inspection Hall, and Incense Hall: three yellow gauze curtains, four yellow gauze valances, one hundred ninety-five panels of yellow silk hangings, thirty-five offering and assisting positions, one hundred purple gauze kneeling mats, two hundred each of rush and reed mats, forty wooden lamp frames, one hundred ten crimson gauze lamp covers, ten red wick lamps, two candle-trimming knives, thirty iron lamp-oil trays with stands, two hundred yellow candles, two hundred miscellaneous candles, three hundred hemp wicks, and one hundred jin each of pine resin and clear oil.
translations.idiomatic: For the Offering Pavilion, Inspection Hall, and Incense Hall the court provided three yellow gauze curtains, four valances, one hundred ninety-five yellow silk panels, thirty-five offering and assisting stations, one hundred purple gauze kneeling mats, two hundred rush mats and two hundred reed mats, forty wooden lamp frames, one hundred ten crimson gauze lamp covers, ten red wick lamps, two candle knives, thirty iron lamp-oil trays on stands, two hundred yellow candles and two hundred general-purpose candles, three hundred hemp wicks, and one hundred jin each of pine resin and clear oil.

sentences.zh: 此饌幕板位燭燎之用也。

translations.literal: These were the supplies for the Offering Pavilion, positions, and lamps and torches.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the furnishings for the offering pavilion, ritual stations, and lighting.

sentences.zh: 初獻官一，亞獻官一，終獻官一，攝司徒一，助奠官二，太常卿一，光祿卿一，廩犧令一，太官令一，巾篚官四，祝史四，監祭御史二，監禮博士二，司天監二，良醞令一，奉爵官一，司尊罍二，盥洗官二，爵洗官二，大社令一，大社丞一，大樂令一，大樂丞一，協律郎二，奉禮郎二，讀祝官一，舉祝官二，奉幣官四，剪燭官二，太祝七，齋郎四十有八，贊者一，禮直官三，與祭官無定員。

translations.literal: One initial offering official, one secondary offering official, one final offering official, one acting Minister of Education, two assisting presentation officials, one Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, one Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, one Director of the Pasturage for Sacrificial Victims, one Director of the Imperial Kitchen, four officials for towels and baskets, four prayer clerks, two supervising sacrifice censors, two supervising ritual erudites, two directors of the Astronomical Bureau, one Director of Fine Brew, one official to present the libation cup, two officials for wine vessels, two hand-washing officials, two cup-washing officials, one Director of the Great Altar of Soil, one Assistant Director of the Great Altar of Soil, one Director of the Grand Music Office, one Assistant Director of the Grand Music Office, two pitch regulators, two ritual presentation officials, one prayer-reading official, two prayer-holding officials, four silk-presenting officials, two candle-trimming officials, seven grand invokers, forty-eight acolytes, one announcer, three ritual ushers, and participating officials without fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: The roster comprised one initial, one secondary, and one final offering official; an acting Minister of Education; two assisting presentation officials; the directors of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, sacrificial pasturage, and the imperial kitchen; four towel-and-basket officials; four prayer clerks; two supervising sacrifice censors and two supervising ritual erudites; two astronomical directors; the director of fine brew; officials to present the cup, tend the wine vessels, perform hand-washing and cup-washing; the director and assistant director of the Great Altar of Soil; the director and assistant director of the Grand Music Office; two pitch regulators and two ritual presentation officials; officials to read and hold the prayer, present silks, and trim candles; seven grand invokers; forty-eight acolytes; one announcer; three ritual ushers; and additional participants without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 此獻攝執事之人也。

translations.literal: These were the persons for the offerings, acting roles, and ritual duties.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the officials who offered, assisted, and performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 凡祭之日，以春秋二仲月上戊。

translations.literal: As a rule, the day of sacrifice was the wu day of the second month of spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were held on the wu day of the second month of spring and of autumn.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年改用中戊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou, they changed to use the middle wu day.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yanyou era (1319), the court switched to the middle wu day of the month.

sentences.zh: 其儀註之節有六：

translations.literal: The ritual procedure had six sections:
translations.idiomatic: The ritual procedure comprised six stages:

sentences.zh: 一曰迎香。

translations.literal: First, Welcoming the Incense.
translations.idiomatic: First: Welcoming the Incense.

sentences.zh: 前一日，有司告諭坊市，灑掃經行衢路，設香案。

translations.literal: On the day before, the responsible officials announced to the wards and markets, sprinkled and swept the thoroughfares along the route, and set out incense tables.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rite, officials notified the wards and markets, swept the processional route, and set out incense tables.

sentences.zh: 至日質明，有司具香酒樓輿，三獻官以下及諸執事官各具公服，五品以下官、齋郎等皆借紫，詣崇天門。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day, the responsible officials prepared incense, wine, and palanquins; the three offering officials and below and all ritual attendants each wore court dress; officials of fifth rank and below and acolytes all borrowed purple robes, and proceeded to Chongtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the appointed day, officials prepared incense, wine, and palanquins. The three offering officials and all ritual attendants wore court dress; officials below fifth rank and the acolytes borrowed purple robes and went to Chongtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 三獻官及太常禮儀院官入，奉祝及禦香、尚尊酒、馬湩自內出。

translations.literal: The three offering officials and officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Protocol entered, and bore out the prayer text, imperial incense, imperial wine, and mare's milk from within.
translations.idiomatic: The three offering officials and officers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Protocol entered the palace and brought out the prayer text, imperial incense, imperial wine, and mare's milk.

sentences.zh: 監祭御史、監禮博士、奉禮郎、太祝分左右兩班前導。

translations.literal: The supervising sacrifice censors, supervising ritual erudites, ritual presentation officials, and grand invokers led the way in two columns, left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censors, ritual erudites, presentation officials, and grand invokers led in two columns to left and right.

sentences.zh: 控鶴五人，一人執傘，四人執儀仗，由大明門正門出。

translations.literal: Five Crane-Handlers, one holding an umbrella and four bearing ceremonial regalia, went out through the main gate of Daming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Five Crane-Handlers followed—one with a parasol, four with ceremonial regalia—out through the main gate of Daming Gate.

sentences.zh: 教坊大樂作。

translations.literal: The grand music of the Music Bureau played.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Bureau struck up the grand music.

sentences.zh: 至崇天門外，奉香酒、馬湩者各安置於輿，導引如儀。

translations.literal: When they reached outside Chongtian Gate, those bearing incense, wine, and mare's milk each placed them on the palanquins, and the procession advanced according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Chongtian Gate, bearers of incense, wine, and mare's milk set them on the palanquins, and the procession moved off as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至紅門外，百官乘馬分班行於儀仗之外，清道官行於儀衛之先，兵馬司巡兵夾道次之，金鼓又次之，京尹儀從左右成列又次之，教坊大樂一隊次之。

translations.literal: When they reached outside Red Gate, the hundred officials mounted horses and marched in formation outside the ceremonial guard; road-clearing officials went before the ceremonial escort; patrol soldiers of the Military Horse Bureau lined the route next; gongs and drums came after them; the metropolitan magistrate's attendants formed columns to left and right after that; and one company of the Music Bureau's grand music came last.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Red Gate the officials mounted and rode in formation beyond the ceremonial guard. Road-clearing officers led the escort; patrol troops lined the route; then came gongs and drums, the metropolitan magistrate's attendants in flanking columns, and finally a company of the Music Bureau's grand ensemble.

sentences.zh: 控鶴弩手各服其服，執儀仗左右成列次之。

translations.literal: Crane-Handlers and crossbowmen, each in his proper dress, bore ceremonial regalia and formed columns to left and right after them.
translations.idiomatic: Crane-Handlers and crossbowmen in full dress followed, bearing regalia in columns to either side.

sentences.zh: 拱衛使行其中，儀鳳司細樂又次之。

translations.literal: The Guardian Commissioner marched in their midst; the refined music of the Ceremonial Phoenix Office came after them.
translations.idiomatic: The Guardian Commissioner marched among them, with the Ceremonial Phoenix Office's refined music behind.

sentences.zh: 太常卿與博士御史導於輿前，獻官、司徒、助奠官從於輿後。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, with erudites and censors, led before the palanquins; the offering officials, Minister of Education, and assisting presentation officials followed behind the palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, erudites, and censors led before the palanquins; offering officials, the Minister of Education, and assisting presentation officials followed behind.

sentences.zh: 若駕幸上都，三獻官以下及諸執事官則詣健德門外，皆具公服於香輿前北向立，異位重行。

translations.literal: If the emperor was visiting the Upper Capital, the three offering officials and below and all ritual attendants then went to outside Jiande Gate, all in court dress, standing north-facing before the incense palanquin in separate ranks, row upon row.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at the Upper Capital, the three offering officials and all ritual attendants went to Jiande Gate in court dress and stood facing north before the incense palanquin in ranked rows.

sentences.zh: 俟奉香酒官驛至，太常官受而奉之，各置於輿。

translations.literal: They waited until the officials bearing incense and wine arrived by relay; Imperial Sacrifices officials received and bore them, placing each on a palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: When the relay bearers of incense and wine arrived, officials of Imperial Sacrifices received them and set each item on its palanquin.

sentences.zh: 禮直官贊「班齊」，「鞠躬」，「再拜興」，「平立」。

translations.literal: The ritual usher announced: "Ranks aligned," "Bow," "Bow twice and rise," "Stand level."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual usher called: "Ranks aligned," "Bow," "Bow twice and rise," "Stand at ease."

sentences.zh: 班首稍前搢笏跪，眾官皆跪，三上香，出笏就拜興，平立退復位，北向立，鞠躬，再拜興，平立。

translations.literal: The head of the rank stepped slightly forward, inserted his tablet, and knelt; all officials knelt; incense was offered three times; they withdrew the tablets, bowed and rose, stood level, withdrew and returned to position, stood north-facing, bowed, bowed twice and rose, and stood level.
translations.idiomatic: The lead official stepped forward, inserted his tablet, and knelt; all knelt and offered incense three times; they withdrew their tablets, bowed, rose, and returned to place; facing north they bowed again twice, rose, and stood at ease.

sentences.zh: 眾官上馬，分班前導如儀。

translations.literal: All officials mounted horses and led the way in formation according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The officials mounted and led the procession in formation as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至社稷壇北神門外皆下馬，分左右入自北門，序立如儀。

translations.literal: When they reached outside the Spirit Gate on the north of the Soil and Grain altars, all dismounted, entered by the north gate to left and right, and took their places in order according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the Spirit Gate north of the altars everyone dismounted, entered through the north gate in left and right files, and took their stations as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、博士、御史前導，獻官、司徒、助奠等官後從。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, erudites, and censors led in front; offering officials, the Minister of Education, assisting presentation officials, and the like followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, erudites, and censors led; offering officials, the Minister of Education, and assisting presentation officials followed.

sentences.zh: 至望祀堂下，三獻奉香、酒、馬湩升階，置於堂中黃羅幕下。

translations.literal: When they reached below the Hall for Distant Sacrifice, the three offering officials bore incense, wine, and mare's milk up the steps and placed them beneath the yellow gauze curtain in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hall for Distant Sacrifice the three offering officials carried incense, wine, and mare's milk up the steps and set them under the yellow gauze curtain inside.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引三獻官以次而出，各詣齋次，釋服。

translations.literal: The ritual usher led the three offering officials out in order; each went to the abstinence quarters and changed out of ritual dress.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual usher led the three offering officials out in turn to the abstinence quarters to change out of ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 二曰齋戒。

translations.literal: Second, Abstinence and Purification.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Abstinence and Purification.

sentences.zh: 前期三日質明，有司設三獻官以下行事執事官位於中書省。

translations.literal: At dawn three days before, the responsible officials set the positions of the three offering officials and below and all ritual attendants at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn three days before the rite, officials arranged the stations of the three offering officials and all ritual attendants at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太尉南向，監祭御史位二於其西，東向，監禮博士位二於其東，西向，俱北上。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal faced south; two supervising sacrifice censors were positioned west of him, facing east; two supervising ritual erudites were positioned east of him, facing west; all ranked with the higher to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal faced south. Two supervising sacrifice censors stood to his west, facing east; two supervising ritual erudites to his east, facing west; in each pair the senior man stood to the north.

sentences.zh: 司徒、亞獻、終獻位於其南，北向。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education, the secondary offering official, and the final offering official were positioned south of them, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: South of them stood the Minister of Education, the secondary offering official, and the final offering official, all facing north.

sentences.zh: 次助奠，稍卻。

translations.literal: Next came the assisting presentation officials, set back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The assisting presentation officials stood a step farther back.

sentences.zh: 次太常卿、光祿卿、大官令、司尊彜、良醞令、太社令、廩犧令、光祿丞、大樂令、太社丞。

translations.literal: Next came the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of Imperial Entertainments, Director of the Imperial Kitchen, official for ritual vessels, Director of Fine Brew, Director of the Great Altar of Soil, Director of Sacrificial Pasturage, Assistant Director of Imperial Entertainments, Director of the Grand Music Office, and Assistant Director of the Great Altar of Soil.
translations.idiomatic: Next in rank stood the directors of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, and the imperial kitchen; the ritual-vessel officer; the directors of fine brew, the Great Altar of Soil, and sacrificial pasturage; the assistant director of Imperial Entertainments; and the director and assistant director of the Grand Music Office.

sentences.zh: 次讀祝官、奉爵官、太祝、祝史、奉禮郎、協律郎、司天生、諸執事齋郎。

translations.literal: Next came the prayer-reading official, cup-presenting official, grand invokers, prayer clerks, ritual presentation officials, pitch regulators, astronomical directors, and all ritual attendants and acolytes.
translations.idiomatic: Then came officials to read the prayer and present the cup, the grand invokers and prayer clerks, presentation officials and pitch regulators, astronomical directors, and all ritual attendants and acolytes.

sentences.zh: 每等異位重行，俱北向，西上。

translations.literal: Each grade had separate ranks in rows, all facing north, with the higher to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Each grade formed separate rows, all facing north, senior men to the west.

sentences.zh: 贊者引行事執事官各就位，立定。

translations.literal: The announcer led the ritual-attendant officials each to his position, and they stood in place.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer led each ritual attendant to his station and they took their places.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太尉、初獻就位，讀誓曰：「某年某月某日上戊日，祭於太社太稷，各揚其職，其或不敬，國有常刑。」

translations.literal: The ritual usher led the Grand Marshal and the initial offering official to their positions, and the oath was read: "On such-and-such a year, month, and day, the wu day of the second month, sacrifice is made at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain. Each shall perform his duty; if any is disrespectful, the state has fixed punishments."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual usher led the Grand Marshal and initial offering official to their stations and read the oath: "On [date], the wu day of the second month, we sacrifice at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain. Let each perform his duty; disrespect will be punished by law."

sentences.zh: 散齋二日，宿於正寢，致齋一日於祠所。

translations.literal: There followed two days of preliminary abstinence, lodging in the principal quarters, and one day of full abstinence at the sacrificial site.
translations.idiomatic: Preliminary abstinence lasted two days in the principal quarters; full abstinence one day at the sacrificial site.

sentences.zh: 散齋日治事如故，不吊喪問疾，不作樂，不判署刑殺文字，不決罰罪人，不與穢惡事。

translations.literal: On days of preliminary abstinence, official business was conducted as usual, but without condoling the bereaved or inquiring after the ill, without making music, without signing documents on punishments and executions, without adjudicating and punishing offenders, and without involvement in defiling or foul affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During preliminary abstinence, officials carried on business as usual but did not pay condolence calls or inquire after the sick, make music, sign documents involving capital punishment, judge and punish criminals, or involve themselves in anything unclean.

sentences.zh: 致齋日，惟祭事得行，其餘悉禁。

translations.literal: On days of full abstinence, only sacrificial affairs were permitted; all else was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On full-abstinence days only sacrificial duties were allowed; everything else was prohibited.

sentences.zh: 凡與祭之官已齋而闕者，通攝行事。

translations.literal: For any official participating in the sacrifice who had kept abstinence but was absent, a substitute would act comprehensively in performing the rites.
translations.idiomatic: If a participant who had kept abstinence was absent, another official would substitute for him in performing the rites.

sentences.zh: 七品以下官先退，余官對拜。

translations.literal: Officials of the seventh rank and below withdrew first; the remaining officials bowed facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of seventh rank and below withdrew first; the rest exchanged facing bows.

sentences.zh: 守壝門兵衛與大樂工人，俱清齋一日。

translations.literal: The guards defending the enclosure gates and the workers of the Grand Music Office all kept pure abstinence for one day.
translations.idiomatic: Gate guards and Grand Music Office workers each kept one day of pure abstinence.

sentences.zh: 行禮官，前期習儀於祠所。

translations.literal: The ritual-performing officials rehearsed the ceremony at the sacrificial site in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand, ritual officers rehearsed the ceremony at the sacrificial site.

sentences.zh: 三曰陳設。

translations.literal: Third: Arranging the installations.
translations.idiomatic: Third: Arranging the installations.

sentences.zh: 前期三日，所司設三獻以下行事執事官次於齋房之內，又設饌幕四於西神門之外，稍南，西向，北上。

translations.literal: Three days before, the responsible offices set stations for the three offering officials and below and all ritual-attendant officials inside the abstinence chambers, and also set four offering tents outside the western spirit gate, slightly to the south, facing west, with the higher to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before, officials assigned stations within the abstinence chambers to the three offering officials and all ritual attendants, and erected four offering tents just south of the western spirit gate, facing west, senior men to the north.

sentences.zh: 今有饌幕殿在西壝門外，近北，南向。

translations.literal: At present there is an offering-tent hall outside the western enclosure gate, near the north, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At present an offering hall stands just outside the western enclosure gate, near the north side, facing south.

sentences.zh: 陳設如儀。

translations.literal: Installations were arranged according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Installations were arranged according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 前祭二日，所司設兵衛，各以其方色器服守衛壝門，每門二人，每隅一人。

translations.literal: Two days before the sacrifice, the responsible offices posted military guards, each wearing the equipment and accoutrements of his directional color to guard the enclosure gates—two men at each gate, one at each corner.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before sacrifice, guards in directional colors and regalia were posted at the enclosure gates—two at each gate and one at each corner.

sentences.zh: 大樂令帥其屬設登歌之樂於兩壇上，稍北，南向。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Music Office led his subordinates to set the ascent-and-song music on both altars, slightly to the north, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Music Office stationed ascent-and-song musicians on both altars, slightly to the north and facing south.

sentences.zh: 磬虡在東，鐘虡在西，一在鐘虡南稍東，一在磬虡南稍西。

translations.literal: The chime frame was in the east and the bell frame in the west; one was placed slightly east of south of the bell frame, and one slightly west of south of the chime frame.
translations.idiomatic: Chime frames stood to the east and bell frames to the west; one instrument was placed southeast of the bell frame and one southwest of the chime frame.

sentences.zh: 搏拊二，一在南，一在南，東西相向。

translations.literal: Two clappers, one in the south and one in the south, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two clappers, one on the south of each altar, faced each other across the east-west axis.

sentences.zh: 歌工次之，余工位在縣後。

translations.literal: Singers were placed next; the remaining musicians' stations were behind the suspended bells.
translations.idiomatic: Singers stood next; other musicians took their places behind the suspended bells.

sentences.zh: 其匏竹者位於壇下，重行南向，相對為首。

translations.literal: Those with gourd and bamboo instruments were stationed below the altars, in double rows facing south, facing each other as leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and bamboo musicians were arrayed below the altars in double rows facing south, paired leaders facing each other.

sentences.zh: 太社令帥其屬掃除壇之上下，為瘞坎二於壬地，方深足以容物，南出陛。

translations.literal: The Director of the Great Altar of Soil led his subordinates to sweep above and below the altars, and dug two burial pits in the ren position, square and deep enough to hold the offerings, opening south toward the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Great Altar of Soil had his staff sweep the altars and dig two burial pits at the ren position, square pits deep enough for the offerings with openings facing south toward the steps.

sentences.zh: 前祭一日，司天監、太社令帥其屬升，設太社、太稷神座各於壇上，近南，北向。

translations.literal: One day before the sacrifice, the Astronomical Directorate and the Director of the Great Altar of Soil led their subordinates up to set the spirit seats for the Great Altar of Soil and the Great Altar of Grain, each on its altar near the south, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of sacrifice, the Astronomical Directorate and Director of the Great Altar of Soil ascended to set spirit seats for the altars of Soil and Grain near the south of each altar, facing north.

sentences.zh: 設后土神座於太社神座之左，後稷神座於太稷神座之左，俱東向。

translations.literal: The spirit seat for the Spirit of Earth was set to the left of the Great Altar of Soil seat; the spirit seat for Lord of Grain to the left of the Great Altar of Grain seat—both facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The Spirit of Earth's seat was placed to the left of the Soil altar's seat, and Lord of Grain's seat to the left of the Grain altar's seat; both faced east.

sentences.zh: 席皆以莞，裀褥如幣之色，設神位版各於座首。

translations.literal: All mats were of coarse rush; cushions and coverlets matched the color of the silks, and spirit-tablet plaques were set at the head of each seat.
translations.idiomatic: Rush mats were laid, with cushions colored to match the silk offerings, and spirit-tablet plaques placed at the head of each seat.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎設三獻官位於西神門之內道南，亞獻、終獻位稍卻。

translations.literal: The presentation official set the stations of the three offering officials inside the western spirit gate, south of the path; the secondary and final offering officials were placed slightly back.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation official arranged stations for the three offering officials south of the path inside the western spirit gate, with the secondary and final offerers a step farther back.

sentences.zh: 司徒位道北，太常卿、光祿卿次之，稍卻。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education's station was north of the path; the Director of Imperial Sacrifices and Director of Imperial Entertainments came next, set slightly back.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education stood north of the path, with the directors of Imperial Sacrifices and Imperial Entertainments behind him, slightly set back.

sentences.zh: 司天監、光祿丞又次之。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Directorate and Assistant Director of Imperial Entertainments came after them.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Directorate and assistant director of Imperial Entertainments stood still farther back.

sentences.zh: 太社令、大官令、良醞令、廩犧令、太社丞、讀祝官、奉爵官、太祝以次位於其北，諸執事者及祝史、齋郎位於其後。

translations.literal: The Director of the Great Altar of Soil, Director of the Imperial Kitchen, Director of Fine Brew, Director of Sacrificial Pasturage, Assistant Director of the Great Altar of Soil, prayer-reading official, cup-presenting official, and grand invokers were stationed in succession to their north; all ritual attendants, prayer clerks, and acolytes were behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Next to their north stood the directors of the Great Altar of Soil, imperial kitchen, fine brew, and sacrificial pasturage; the assistant director of the Great Altar of Soil; and officials for reading prayers, presenting cups, and invoking; ritual attendants, prayer clerks, and acolytes stood behind them.

sentences.zh: 每等異位重行，俱東向，南上。

translations.literal: Each grade formed separate rows in ranks, all facing east, with the higher to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Each grade formed separate rows facing east, senior men to the south.

sentences.zh: 又設監祭御史位二，監禮博士位二，於太社壇子陛之東北，俱東向，南上。

translations.literal: Two supervising sacrifice censor stations and two supervising ritual erudite stations were also set at the northeast of the subsidiary steps of the Great Altar of Soil altar, all facing east, with the higher to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising sacrifice censors and two supervising ritual erudites were also posted northeast of the Soil altar's subsidiary steps, facing east with senior men to the south.

sentences.zh: 設奉禮郎位於稷壇之西北隅，贊者位於東北隅，俱東向。

translations.literal: The presentation official's station was set at the northwest corner of the Grain altar; the announcer's at the northeast corner—both facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation official stood at the northwest corner of the Grain altar and the announcer at the northeast corner, both facing east.

sentences.zh: 協律郎位二，於各壇上樂虡東北，俱南向。

translations.literal: Two pitch regulators' stations were set at the northeast of the music frames on each altar, all facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Two pitch regulators were posted northeast of the music frames on each altar, facing south.

sentences.zh: 太樂令位於兩壇樂虡之間南向，司尊彜位於酌尊所，俱南向。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Music Office was stationed between the music frames of the two altars, facing south; the official for ritual vessels at the libation-vessel station—both facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Music Office stood between the altars' music frames, facing south, as did the ritual-vessel officer at the libation station.

sentences.zh: 設望瘞位於坎之南，北向。

translations.literal: A station for gazing at the burial pit was set south of the pit, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: A station for watching the burial offering was placed south of the pit, facing north.

sentences.zh: 又設牲榜於西神門外，東向。

translations.literal: A victim roster was also set outside the western spirit gate, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: A victim roster was also posted outside the western spirit gate, facing east.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝位於牲西，祝史次之，東向。

translations.literal: The grand invokers were stationed west of the victims; prayer clerks came next; all faced east.
translations.idiomatic: Grand invokers stood west of the victims with prayer clerks behind them, all facing east.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、光祿卿、大官令位在南，北向，東上。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of Imperial Entertainments, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen were stationed in the south, facing north, with the higher to the east.
translations.idiomatic: The directors of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, and the imperial kitchen stood to the south facing north, senior men to the east.

sentences.zh: 監祭、監禮位於太常卿之東稍卻，俱北向，東上。

translations.literal: The supervising sacrifice and supervising ritual officials were placed east of the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, slightly set back, all facing north, with the higher to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising sacrifice and ritual officials stood east of the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, slightly set back, all facing north with senior men to the east.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令位於牲東北，南向。

translations.literal: The Director of Sacrificial Pasturage was stationed northeast of the victims, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Pasturage stood northeast of the victims, facing south.

sentences.zh: 又設禮饌於牲東，設省饌於禮饌之北，今有省饌殿設位於其北，東西相向，南上。

translations.literal: Ritual offerings were also set east of the victims, and inspection offerings north of the ritual offerings; at present there is an inspection-offering hall with stations set to its north, facing each other east and west, with the higher to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual offerings were placed east of the victims and inspection offerings north of them; at present an inspection hall north of these has facing stations east and west, senior men to the south.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、光祿卿、大官令位於西，東向，監祭、監禮位於東，西向，俱南上，禮部設版案各於神位之側，司尊彜、奉禮郎帥執事者設玉幣篚於酌尊所。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of Imperial Entertainments, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen were stationed in the west, facing east; supervising sacrifice and supervising ritual officials in the east, facing west—all with the higher to the south; the Ministry of Rites set tablet cases at the sides of each spirit seat; the official for ritual vessels and the presentation official led attendants to set jade-and-silk baskets at the libation station.
translations.idiomatic: The directors of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, and the imperial kitchen stood in the west facing east; supervising sacrifice and ritual officials in the east facing west, senior men to the south; the Ministry of Rites placed tablet cases beside each spirit seat; the ritual-vessel officer and presentation official had attendants set jade-and-silk baskets at the libation station.

sentences.zh: 次設籩豆之位，每位各籩十、豆十、簠二、簋二、铏三、俎五、盤一。

translations.literal: Next they set the stations for platters and stands: at each seat ten platters, ten stands, two grain vessels, two millet vessels, three soup vessels, five meat stands, and one tray.
translations.idiomatic: Next platters and stands were arranged—ten of each per seat, plus two grain vessels, two millet vessels, three soup vessels, five meat stands, and one tray.

sentences.zh: 又各設籩一、豆一、簠一、簋一、俎三於饌幕內。

translations.literal: One platter, one stand, one grain vessel, one millet vessel, and three meat stands were also set for each inside the offering tents.
translations.idiomatic: Each offering tent also received one platter, one stand, one grain vessel, one millet vessel, and three meat stands.

sentences.zh: 毛血別置一豆。

translations.literal: Fur and blood were separately placed in one stand.
translations.idiomatic: Fur and blood were set aside in a separate stand.

sentences.zh: 設尊罍之位，社稷正位各太尊二、著尊二、犧尊二、山罍二，於壇上酉陛之西北隅，南向，東上。

translations.literal: Stations for wine vessels and libation jars were set: at each principal seat of the altars of Soil and Grain, two Grand Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, and two Mountain Jars, at the northwest corner of the you steps on the altar, facing south, with the higher to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Wine vessels were placed at each principal Soil and Grain seat—two Grand, Display, and Sacrificial Vessels and two Mountain Jars—at the northwest corner of the you steps on the altar, facing south with senior vessels to the east.

sentences.zh: 設配位各著尊二、犧尊二、象尊二、山罍二，在正位酒尊之西，俱南向，東上。

translations.literal: For associated seats, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, and two Mountain Jars were set west of the principal wine vessels, all facing south, with the higher to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Associated seats received two Display, Sacrificial, and Elephant Vessels and two Mountain Jars west of the principal wine vessels, all facing south, senior vessels to the east.

sentences.zh: 又設正位各象尊二、壺尊二、山罍二，於壇下子陛之東，南向，東上。

translations.literal: Two Elephant Vessels, two Pot Vessels, and two Mountain Jars were also set for each principal seat east of the zi steps below the altar, facing south, with the higher to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Each principal seat also had two Elephant and Pot Vessels and two Mountain Jars east of the zi steps below the altar, facing south with senior vessels to the east.

sentences.zh: 配位各壺尊二、山罍二，在卯陛之南，西向，南上。

translations.literal: Associated seats each had two Pot Vessels and two Mountain Jars, south of the mao steps, facing west, with the higher to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Associated seats had two Pot Vessels and two Mountain Jars south of the mao steps, facing west with senior vessels to the south.

sentences.zh: 又設洗位二，於各壇子陛之西北，南向。

translations.literal: Two hand-washing stations were also set at the northwest of the subsidiary steps of each altar, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Two hand-washing stations were also placed northwest of each altar's subsidiary steps, facing south.

sentences.zh: 篚在洗東北肆，執罍篚者各位於其後。

translations.literal: Baskets were set out northeast of the washing stations, and the attendants holding jars and baskets each took stations behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Baskets were arrayed northeast of the washing stations, with jar and basket attendants stationed behind them.

sentences.zh: 祭日醜前五刻，司天監、太社令各服其服，帥其屬升，設正配位神位版於壇上。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, five quarters before the chou hour, the Astronomical Directorate and the Director of the Great Altar of Soil each donned proper dress, led their subordinates up, and set the spirit-tablet plaques for principal and associated seats on the altars.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of sacrifice, five quarters before the chou hour, the Astronomical Directorate and Director of the Great Altar of Soil, in full dress, ascended to set spirit-tablet plaques for principal and associated seats on the altars.

sentences.zh: 又陳玉幣，正位禮神之玉一，兩圭有邸，置於匣。

translations.literal: Jade and silks were also displayed; for each principal seat one jade for honoring the spirit—a double-blade tablet with base—placed in its case.
translations.idiomatic: Jade and silks were also displayed; each principal seat received a double-blade spirit jade with base, kept in its case.

sentences.zh: 正配位幣皆以玄，各長一丈八尺，陳於篚。

translations.literal: Silks for principal and associated seats were all black, each eighteen feet long, displayed in baskets.
translations.idiomatic: Principal and associated silks were all black, eighteen feet long, laid out in baskets.

sentences.zh: 太祝取瘞玉加於幣，實於篚，瘞玉以玉石為之，及禮神之玉各置於神座前。

translations.literal: The grand invoker took the burial jade and added it to the silks, placing them in the basket; the burial jade was made of stone and jade, and together with the spirit-honoring jades each was placed before its spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Grand invokers added burial jade to the silks and placed them in baskets; the stone burial jades and spirit jades were each set before the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿帥其屬，入實籩豆簠簋。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Entertainments led his subordinates to fill the platters, stands, grain vessels, and millet vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Entertainments had his staff fill the platters, stands, and grain and millet vessels.

sentences.zh: 每位籩三行，以右為上。

translations.literal: At each seat the platters were in three rows, with the right as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Each seat had platters in three rows, ranked with right as superior.

sentences.zh: 第一行，乾䕩在前，乾棗、形鹽、魚鱐次之。

translations.literal: First row: dried 䕩 first, then dried dates, molded salt, and dried salted fish.
translations.idiomatic: First row: dried 䕩, then dried dates, molded salt, and dried salted fish.

sentences.chineseCharacterReason: Rare ritual food term preserved because the graph 䕩 is opaque and prior English renderings were inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 第二行，鹿脯在前，榛實、乾桃次之。

translations.literal: Second row: venison jerky first, then hazel nuts and dried peaches.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: venison jerky, then hazelnuts and dried peaches.

sentences.zh: 第三行，菱在前，芡、栗次之。

translations.literal: Third row: water chestnuts first, then gorgon fruit and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: Third row: water chestnuts, then gorgon fruit and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 豆三行，以左為上。

translations.literal: The stands were in three rows, with the left as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Stands were arranged in three rows, with left as superior.

sentences.zh: 第一行，芹菹在前，筍菹、葵菹、菁菹次之。

translations.literal: First row: pickled celery first, then pickled bamboo shoots, pickled mallow, and pickled smartweed.
translations.idiomatic: First row: pickled celery, then pickled bamboo shoots, mallow, and smartweed.

sentences.zh: 第二行，韭菹在前，魚醢、兔醢次之。

translations.literal: Second row: pickled leeks first, then fish paste and rabbit paste.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: pickled leeks, then fish and rabbit paste.

sentences.zh: 第三行，豚拍在前，鹿臡、醓醢次之。

translations.literal: Third row: pork ribs first, then minced venison and seasoned meat paste.
translations.idiomatic: Third row: pork ribs, then minced venison and seasoned meat paste.

sentences.zh: 簠實以稻粱，簋實以黍稷，铏實以羹。

translations.literal: The grain vessels were filled with rice and millet; the millet vessels with panicled millet and grain; the soup vessels with broth.
translations.idiomatic: Grain vessels held rice and millet, millet vessels held panicled millet and grain, and soup vessels held broth.

sentences.zh: 良醞令帥其屬，入實尊罍。

translations.literal: The Director of Fine Brew led his subordinates to fill the wine vessels and libation jars.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Fine Brew had his staff fill the wine vessels and libation jars.

sentences.zh: 正位太尊為上，實以泛齊，著尊實以醴齊，犧尊實以盎齊，象尊實以醍齊，壺尊實以沈齊，山罍實以三酒。

translations.literal: For principal seats the Grand Vessel ranked highest, filled with fan qi; the Display Vessel with li qi; the Sacrificial Vessel with ang qi; the Elephant Vessel with ti qi; the Pot Vessel with chen qi; and the Mountain Jar with the three wines.
translations.idiomatic: At principal seats the Grand Vessel ranked highest with fan qi, followed by Display with li qi, Sacrificial with ang qi, Elephant with ti qi, Pot with chen qi, and Mountain Jar with the three wines.

sentences.zh: 配位著尊為上，實以泛齊，犧尊實以醴齊，象尊實以盎齊，壺尊實以醍齊，山罍實以三酒。

translations.literal: For associated seats the Display Vessel ranked highest, filled with fan qi; the Sacrificial Vessel with li qi; the Elephant Vessel with ang qi; the Pot Vessel with ti qi; and the Mountain Jar with the three wines.
translations.idiomatic: At associated seats the Display Vessel ranked highest with fan qi, followed by Sacrificial with li qi, Elephant with ang qi, Pot with ti qi, and Mountain Jar with the three wines.

sentences.zh: 凡齊之上尊實以明水，酒之上尊實以玄酒，酒齊皆以尚醞代之。

translations.literal: For fermented brews, the highest vessel was filled with clear water; for wines, the highest vessel with dark ale; all fermented brews and wines were replaced by imperial brew.
translations.idiomatic: Highest vessels for fermented brews held clear water, highest wine vessels held dark ale, and all brews and wines were replaced with imperial brew.

sentences.zh: 太常卿設燭於神座前。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices set candles before the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices placed candles before the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 四曰省牲器。

translations.literal: Fourth: Inspecting victims and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Inspecting victims and vessels.

sentences.zh: 前期一日午後八刻，諸衛之屬禁止行人。

translations.literal: One day before, at the eighth quarter after noon, the guards of the various commands forbade travelers.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of sacrifice, at the eighth quarter after noon, guards barred all passersby.

sentences.zh: 未後二刻，太社令帥其屬，掃除壇之上下。

translations.literal: At the second quarter after wei, the Director of the Great Altar of Soil led his subordinates to sweep above and below the altars.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter after wei, the Director of the Great Altar of Soil had his staff sweep the altars.

sentences.zh: 司尊彜、奉禮郎帥執事者，以祭器入設於位。

translations.literal: The official for ritual vessels and the presentation official led attendants to bring the sacrificial vessels in and set them at their stations.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual-vessel officer and presentation official led attendants to carry sacrificial vessels in and set them in place.

sentences.zh: 司天監、太社令升，設神位版及禮神之玉幣如儀。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Directorate and the Director of the Great Altar of Soil ascended to set the spirit-tablet plaques and jades and silks for honoring the spirit according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Directorate and Director of the Great Altar of Soil ascended to set spirit tablets and spirit jades and silks according to protocol.

sentences.zh: 俟告潔畢，權徹，祭日重設。

translations.literal: When the announcement of purity was finished, they were temporarily removed and reset on the sacrifice day.
translations.idiomatic: After the purity announcement they were temporarily removed and reset on the day of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 未後二刻，廩犧令與諸太祝、祝史以牲就位，禮直官、贊者分引太常卿、監祭、監禮、大官令於西神門外省牲位，立定。

translations.literal: At the second quarter after wei, the Director of Sacrificial Pasturage and the grand invokers and prayer clerks brought the victims into place; the ritual usher and announcers separately led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, supervising sacrifice and ritual officials, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen to the victim-inspection station outside the western spirit gate, where they stood in place.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter after wei, the Director of Sacrificial Pasturage and grand invokers and prayer clerks brought the victims into place; ritual ushers and announcers led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, supervising officials, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen to the victim-inspection station outside the western spirit gate.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿，贊者引監祭、監禮，入自西神門，詣太社壇，自西陛升，視滌濯於上，執事者皆舉冪曰「潔」。

translations.literal: The ritual usher led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, and the announcers led the supervising sacrifice and ritual officials; entering through the western spirit gate they proceeded to the Great Altar of Soil, ascended by the west steps, and inspected the washing above; all attendants raised the covers and called out "Pure."
translations.idiomatic: A ritual usher led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices while announcers led supervising officials through the western spirit gate to the Soil altar; ascending the west steps they inspected the washing, and attendants raised covers and called, "Pure."

sentences.zh: 次詣太稷壇，如太社之儀訖，降復位。

translations.literal: Next they proceeded to the Great Altar of Grain and performed the same rite as at the Great Altar of Soil; when finished they descended and returned to their stations.
translations.idiomatic: They next proceeded to the Grain altar and performed the same rite; when finished they descended and returned to their stations.

sentences.zh: 禮直官稍前曰「告潔畢，請省牲」，引太常卿稍前省牲訖，退復位。

translations.literal: The ritual usher stepped slightly forward and said, "The announcement of purity is complete—please inspect the victims," and led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices slightly forward to inspect the victims; when finished he withdrew and returned to his station.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly stepped forward: "Purity announced—inspect the victims," and led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices forward to inspect them before returning to his station.

sentences.zh: 次引廩犧令出班巡牲一匝，東向折身曰「充」，復位。

translations.literal: Next the Director of Sacrificial Pasturage was led out of rank to make one circuit of the victims; turning eastward he bowed and said, "Full," then returned to his station.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Pasturage was led out to circle the victims once; facing east he bowed and declared, "Full," then returned to his station.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝俱巡牲一匝，上一員出班東向折身曰「腯」，復位。

translations.literal: All the grand invokers together made one circuit of the victims; the senior one stepped out of rank, turned eastward, bowed, and said, "Fat," then returned to his station.
translations.idiomatic: Grand invokers circled the victims together; the senior man stepped forward, faced east, bowed, and declared, "Fat," then returned.

sentences.zh: 禮直官稍前曰「省牲畢，請就省饌位」，引太常卿以下各就位，立定。

translations.literal: The ritual usher stepped slightly forward and said, "Victim inspection is complete—please proceed to the offering-inspection stations," and led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices and those below him each to his station, where they stood in place.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly announced, "Victim inspection complete—proceed to offering inspection," and led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices and the others to their stations.

sentences.zh: 省饌畢，還齋所。

translations.literal: When offering inspection was finished, they returned to the abstinence quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After inspecting the offerings they returned to the abstinence quarters.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令與太祝、祝史以次牽牲詣廚，授大官令。

translations.literal: The Director of Sacrificial Pasturage, with the grand invokers and prayer clerks, in succession led the victims to the kitchen and handed them over to the Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Pasturage with grand invokers and prayer clerks led the victims in turn to the kitchen and delivered them to the Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 次引光祿卿以下詣廚省鼎鑊，視滌溉畢，乃還齋所。

translations.literal: Next the Director of Imperial Entertainments and those below him were led to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and pots; when the washing and rinsing had been viewed and finished, they returned to the abstinence quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Entertainments and others were led to inspect the kitchen cauldrons; when washing and rinsing were checked they returned to the abstinence quarters.

sentences.zh: 晡後一刻，大官令帥宰人以鸞刀割牲，祝史以豆取血各置於饌幕。

translations.literal: At the first quarter after the shen period, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen led butchers to cut the victims with the bell-bladed knife; prayer clerks took blood with stands and placed it in each offering tent.
translations.idiomatic: At the first quarter after shen, the Director of the Imperial Kitchen had butchers cut the victims with sacred knives while prayer clerks collected blood in stands and placed it in the offering tents.

sentences.zh: 祝史又取瘞血貯於盤，遂烹牲。

translations.literal: The prayer clerks also took burial blood, stored it in trays, and then the victims were cooked.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer clerks also collected blood for burial in trays, then the victims were cooked.

sentences.zh: 五曰奠玉幣。

translations.literal: Fifth: Presenting jade and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Presenting jade and silks.

sentences.zh: 祭日醜前五刻，三獻官以下行事執事官，各服其服。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, five quarters before the chou hour, the three offering officials and all ritual-attendant officials below them each donned proper dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of sacrifice, five quarters before the chou hour, the three offering officials and all ritual attendants donned full dress.

sentences.zh: 有司設神位版，陳玉幣，實籩豆簠簋尊罍。

translations.literal: The responsible offices set the spirit-tablet plaques, displayed the jades and silks, and filled the platters, stands, grain vessels, millet vessels, wine vessels, and libation jars.
translations.idiomatic: Officials set spirit tablets, displayed jades and silks, and filled platters, stands, grain and millet vessels, and wine jars.

sentences.zh: 俟監祭、監禮按視壇之上下，及徹去蓋冪。

translations.literal: They waited for the supervising sacrifice and supervising ritual officials to inspect above and below the altars and to remove the covers.
translations.idiomatic: They waited while supervising sacrifice and ritual officials inspected the altars and removed vessel covers.

sentences.zh: 未明二刻，大樂令帥工人入，奉禮郎、贊者入就位，禮直官、贊者入就位。

translations.literal: At the second quarter before dawn, the Director of the Grand Music Office led the workers in; the presentation officials and announcers entered and took their stations; the ritual ushers and announcers entered and took their stations.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter before dawn, the Director of the Grand Music Office led musicians in while presentation officials, announcers, and ritual ushers took their stations.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、贊者分引監祭、監禮、諸太祝、祝史、齋郎及諸執事官，自西神門南偏門入，當太社壇北墉下，重行南向立，以東為上。

translations.literal: Ritual ushers and announcers separately led the supervising sacrifice and ritual officials, all grand invokers, prayer clerks, acolytes, and all ritual-attendant officials in through the southern side gate of the western spirit gate; below the north wall of the Great Altar of Soil they stood in double rows facing south, with the east as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers and announcers led supervising officials, grand invokers, prayer clerks, acolytes, and all attendants in through the south side gate of the western spirit gate; below the north wall of the Soil altar they formed double rows facing south, senior men to the east.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰「再拜」，贊者承傳，監祭、監禮以下皆再拜。

translations.literal: The presentation official said, "Bow twice," and the announcers passed the word; the supervising sacrifice and ritual officials and all below bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation official called, "Bow twice," announcers relayed the command, and supervising officials and all below bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 次贊者分引各就壇上下位，祝史奉盤血，太祝奉玉幣，由西階升壇，各於尊所立。

translations.literal: Next the announcers separately led each man to his station above or below the altar; prayer clerks bore tray-blood, grand invokers bore jades and silks, and ascended the altars by the west steps, each standing at the wine-vessel station.
translations.idiomatic: Announcers then led each man to his station; prayer clerks carried blood in trays and grand invokers carried jades and silks, ascending the west steps to stand at the wine-vessel stations.

sentences.zh: 次引監祭、監禮按視壇之上下，糾察不如儀者，退復位。

translations.literal: Next the supervising sacrifice and supervising ritual officials were led to inspect above and below the altars, to discipline those not conforming to ritual, then withdrew and returned to their stations.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising officials inspected the altars, corrected any lapses in protocol, then returned to their stations.

sentences.zh: 質明，禮直官、贊者各引三獻以下行禮執事官入就位，皆由西神門南偏門以入。

translations.literal: At dawn, ritual ushers and announcers each led the three offering officials and below and all ritual-performing attendant officials in to their stations, all entering by the southern side gate of the western spirit gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn ushers and announcers led the three offering officials and all ritual attendants to their stations through the south side gate of the western spirit gate.

sentences.zh: 禮直官進初獻之左，曰「有司謹具，請行事」，退復位。

translations.literal: The ritual usher advanced to the left of the initial offering official and said, "The officials have reverently prepared everything—please perform the rite," then withdrew and returned to his station.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual usher stepped to the initial offerer's left and announced, "All is prepared—begin the rite," then withdrew to his station.

sentences.zh: 協律郎跪，俯伏舉麾興，工鼓，樂作八成，偃麾，戛樂止。

translations.literal: The pitch regulator knelt, prostrated, raised the banner, and rose; the craftsmen beat the drums; music began in eight sections; the banner was lowered, the wooden clapper sounded, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch regulator knelt, prostrated, raised the banner, and rose; craftsmen beat the drums; music played through eight sections; the banner fell, the clapper sounded, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿瘞血於坎訖，復位，祝史以盤還饌幕，以俟奉毛血豆。

translations.literal: The ritual usher led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices to bury the blood in the pit; when finished he returned to his station; prayer clerks with trays returned to the food canopy to await bearing the hair-and-blood dou.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual usher led the Director of Imperial Sacrifices to bury the blood in the pit, then returned to station; prayer clerks carried trays back to the food canopy to await presenting the hair-and-blood dou.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰「眾官再拜」，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The presentation official said, "All officials, bow twice," and all in station bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation official called, "All officials, bow twice," and everyone in station bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 又贊諸執事者各就位，禮直官、贊者分引執事官各就壇上下位。

translations.literal: He again announced that all ritual attendants should each take their stations; ritual ushers and announcers separately led the attendant officials each to his station above or below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: He called again for all attendants to take their stations; ushers and announcers led each official to his place above or below the altar.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝各取玉幣於篚，立於尊所。

translations.literal: Each grand invoker took jades and silks from the basket and stood at the wine-vessel station.
translations.idiomatic: Each grand invoker took jades and silks from the basket and stood at the wine station.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引初獻詣太社壇盥洗位，樂作，至位南向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The ritual usher led the initial offerer to the hand-washing station at the Great Altar of Soil; music began; when he reached his station he stood south-facing; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual usher led the initial offerer to the hand-washing station at the Soil altar; music began; at his station he stood facing south; the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 搢笏，盥手，帨手，執笏詣壇，樂作，升自北陛，至壇上，樂止。

translations.literal: He inserted his tablet, washed his hands, dried them, took up his tablet, and proceeded to the altar; music began; he ascended by the north steps to the top of the altar; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He washed and dried his hands, went to the altar as music began, ascended the north steps to the top, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 詣太社神座前，南向立，樂作，搢笏跪。

translations.literal: He proceeded before the spirit seat of the Great Altar of Soil, stood south-facing; music began; he inserted his tablet and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: He came before the Soil altar's spirit seat, stood facing south; music began, and he knelt with tablet in hand.

sentences.zh: 太祝加玉於幣，東向跪以授初獻，初獻受玉幣奠訖，執笏俯伏興，少退，再拜訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The grand invoker set jade with the silks and, kneeling east-facing, handed them to the initial offerer; the initial offerer received the jades and silks and presented them; when finished he took up his tablet, prostrated, and rose, withdrew slightly, bowed twice; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The grand invoker set jade with the silks and, kneeling east, handed them to the initial offerer; he received and presented them, prostrated and rose, withdrew slightly, bowed twice, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引初獻降自北陛，詣太稷壇盥洗位，樂作，至位樂止。

translations.literal: The ritual usher led the initial offerer down by the north steps and to the hand-washing station at the Great Altar of Grain; music began; when he reached his station the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual usher led the initial offerer down the north steps to the hand-washing station at the Grain altar; music played until he reached his station, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 盥洗訖，升壇奠玉幣，並如太社后土之儀。

translations.literal: When hand-washing was finished, he ascended the altar and presented jades and silks—all by the same rite as at the Great Altar of Soil and the Spirit of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: After washing, he ascended and presented jades and silks by the same rite as at the Soil altar and Spirit of Earth.

sentences.zh: 奠畢，降自北陛，樂作，復位樂止。

translations.literal: When presentation was finished, he descended by the north steps; music began; when he returned to his station the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation was done, he descended the north steps, returned to station as music played, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 初獻奠玉幣將畢，祝史各奉毛血豆立於西神門外，俟奠玉幣畢，樂止。

translations.literal: As the initial offerer's presentation of jades and silks was nearly finished, prayer clerks each bore the hair-and-blood dou and stood outside the western spirit gate, awaiting the completion of the jade-and-silk presentation; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: As the initial offerer neared the end of presenting jades and silks, prayer clerks with hair-and-blood dou stood outside the western spirit gate; when the presentation was complete the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 祝史奉正位毛血入自中門，配位毛血入自偏門，至壇下，正位者升自北陛，配位者升自西陛，諸太祝迎取於壇上，各進奠於神位前，太祝、祝史俱退立於尊所。

translations.literal: Prayer clerks bearing hair-and-blood for the principal seat entered by the central gate; those for the associated seat entered by the side gate; reaching the foot of the altar, the principal bearers ascended by the north steps and the associated bearers by the west steps; grand invokers met and received them on the altar, each advancing to present before the spirit seat; grand invokers and prayer clerks all withdrew and stood at the wine-vessel station.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer clerks bore principal hair-and-blood in through the central gate and associated blood through the side gate; principal bearers ascended the north steps and associated bearers the west steps; grand invokers met them on the altar and presented before each spirit seat, then all withdrew to the wine station.

sentences.zh: 六曰進熟。

translations.literal: Sixth: Presenting the cooked offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Presenting the cooked offerings.

sentences.zh: 初獻既奠玉幣，有司先陳鼎入於神廚，各在於鑊右。

translations.literal: After the initial offerer had presented jades and silks, the responsible offices first set out tripods in the spirit kitchen, each to the right of its cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Once the initial offerer had presented jades and silks, officers set out tripods in the spirit kitchen, each beside its cauldron.

sentences.zh: 大官令出，帥進饌者詣廚，以匕升羊豕於鑊，各實於一鼎，冪之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen came forth and led those bringing food to the kitchen; with ladles they lifted sheep and pig from the cauldrons, filling each into a tripod and covering them.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen director led food-bearers to the kitchen, ladled sheep and pig from the cauldrons into separate tripods, and covered them.

sentences.zh: 祝史以扃對舉鼎，有司執匕以從，各陳於饌幕內。
