translations.idiomatic: He took the cup and raised the cover; li qi was poured from the elephant vessel and handed to an attendant; he withdrew his tablet, went before the east wing spirit seat, and at station: "Stand facing east, step slightly forward."

sentences.zh: 搢笏跪，三上香，執爵三祭酒，奠爵，出笏，就拜興，平身稍退，鞠躬，拜興，拜興，平身，退復位。

translations.literal: He inserted his tablet and knelt, thrice offered incense, took the cup and thrice libated, set down the cup, withdrew his tablet, prostrated, bowed, and rose, stood at ease and withdrew slightly, bowed from the waist, bowed and rose, bowed and rose, stood at ease, and withdrew to his station.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt, thrice offered incense, thrice libated, set down the cup, prostrated and rose, stood at ease, withdrew slightly, bowed from the waist twice, stood at ease, and returned to station.

sentences.zh: 至階，曰「降階」，至位，曰「就位，西向立」。

translations.literal: Reaching the steps he said, "Descend the steps"; at his station he said, "Take your station, stand west-facing."
translations.idiomatic: At the steps: "Descend"; at station: "Take your place, stand facing west."

sentences.zh: 引西廡分奠官同上儀，唯至神位前，東向立作西向立。

translations.literal: The west wing distribution official followed the same rite, except that at the spirit seat "Stand east-facing" became "Stand west-facing."
translations.idiomatic: The west wing distribution official followed the same rite, except that at the spirit seat he stood west-facing instead of east-facing.

sentences.zh: 俟終獻十哲，兩廡分奠官同時復位。

translations.literal: When the final offering to the Ten Sages was completed, the east and west wing distribution officials returned to their stations at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Once the final offering to the Ten Sages was done, the distribution officials of both wings returned to station together.

sentences.zh: 明贊唱曰「禮饌者徹籩豆」。

translations.literal: The lead announcer intoned, "Meal stewards, remove the baskets and dishes."
translations.idiomatic: The lead announcer called, "Meal stewards, remove the baskets and dishes."

sentences.zh: 徹豆之樂作，禮饌者跪，移先聖前籩豆，略離席，樂止。

translations.literal: Music for removing the dishes began; the meal stewards knelt, moved the baskets and dishes before the Prior Sage, stepped slightly from their seats, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Music for clearing the dishes began; the meal stewards knelt, removed the baskets and dishes before the Prior Sage, stepped back slightly from their seats, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 明贊唱曰「諸執事者退復位」。

translations.literal: The lead announcer intoned, "All attendants, withdraw and return to your stations."
translations.idiomatic: The lead announcer called, "All attendants, withdraw and return to station."

sentences.zh: 俟諸執事者至版位立定，送神之樂作。

translations.literal: When the attendants had reached their rank stations and stood firm, music for sending off the spirits began.
translations.idiomatic: Once attendants had taken their rank stations, music for sending off the spirits began.

sentences.zh: 明贊唱曰「初獻官以下皆再拜」，承傳贊曰「鞠躬，拜，興，拜，興，平身」。

translations.literal: The lead announcer intoned, "All from the initial offering official down, bow twice," and the relay announcer said, "Bow from the waist, bow, rise, bow, rise, stand at ease."
translations.idiomatic: The lead announcer called for all below the initial offerer to bow twice, and the relay announcer guided the bows: "Bow from the waist, bow, rise, bow, rise, stand at ease."

sentences.zh: 樂止。

translations.literal: The music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased.

sentences.zh: 明贊唱曰「祝人取祝，幣人取幣，詣瘞坎」。

translations.literal: The lead announcer intoned, "Invocation reader, take the invocation; silk steward, take the silks; proceed to the burial pit."
translations.idiomatic: The lead announcer called, "Invocation reader, take the invocation; silk steward, take the silks; proceed to the burial pit."

sentences.zh: 俟徹祝幣者出殿門，北向立。

translations.literal: When those removing the invocation and silks had passed out the hall gate, they stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Once those carrying away the invocation and silks had left the hall gate, they stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 望瘞之樂作。

translations.literal: Music for the distant burial began.
translations.idiomatic: Music for the distant burial began.

sentences.zh: 明贊唱曰「三獻官詣望瘞位」，引贊者進前曰「請詣望瘞位」。

translations.literal: The lead announcer intoned, "The three offering officials proceed to the distant-burial station," and an usher-announcer advanced and said, "Please proceed to the distant-burial station."
translations.idiomatic: The lead announcer called the three offering officials to the distant-burial station; an usher-announcer stepped forward: "Please proceed to the distant-burial station."

sentences.zh: 至位，曰「就位，北向立」，曰「可瘞」。

translations.literal: At the station he said, "Take your station, stand north-facing," and said, "You may bury."
translations.idiomatic: At station: "Take your place, stand facing north"; then, "You may bury."

sentences.zh: 埋畢，曰「退，復位」。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, he said, "Withdraw and return to station."
translations.idiomatic: When burial was complete, he called, "Withdraw and return to station."

sentences.zh: 至殿庭前，候樂止，明贊唱曰「典樂官以樂工出就位」，明贊唱曰「闔戶」。

translations.literal: Reaching the front of the hall court, they waited for the music to stop; the lead announcer intoned, "Director of Music, lead the musicians out to their stations," and the lead announcer intoned, "Close the doors."
translations.idiomatic: At the front of the hall court they waited for the music to cease; the lead announcer called the Director of Music to lead the musicians out to station, then called, "Close the doors."

sentences.zh: 又唱曰「初獻官以下退詣圓揖位」，引贊者引獻官退詣圓揖位。

translations.literal: He intoned again, "All from the initial offering official down, withdraw to the circular-bow station," and usher-announcers led the offering officials to withdraw to the circular-bow station.
translations.idiomatic: He called again for all below the initial offerer to withdraw to the circular-bow station, and usher-announcers led the offering officials there.

sentences.zh: 至位，初獻在西，亞終獻及分獻以下在東，陪位官東班在東，西班在西。

translations.literal: At their stations, the initial offerer stood on the west; the secondary and final offerers and distribution officials below stood on the east; attending officials of the eastern rank stood on the east and those of the western rank on the west.
translations.idiomatic: At station the initial offerer stood on the west; the secondary and final offerers and all distribution officials below stood on the east; attending officials of the eastern rank stood east and those of the western rank west.

sentences.zh: 俟立定，明贊唱曰「圓揖」。

translations.literal: When all had stood firm, the lead announcer intoned, "Circular bow."
translations.idiomatic: Once all stood firm, the lead announcer called, "Circular bow."

sentences.zh: 禮畢，退復位，引贊者各引獻官詣幕次更衣。

translations.literal: When the rite was finished, they withdrew to their stations; each usher-announcer led his offering officials to the curtain pavilion to change robes.
translations.idiomatic: The rite complete, they withdrew to station; each usher-announcer led his offering officials to the curtain pavilion to change robes.

sentences.zh: 其飲福受胙，除國學外，諸處仍依常制。

translations.literal: As for drinking the blessing-wine and receiving sacrificial meat, except at the National Academy, everywhere else still followed the usual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Drinking the blessing-wine and receiving sacrificial meat, except at the National Academy, followed the usual regulations everywhere else.

sentences.zh: 闕里之廟，始自太宗九年，令先聖五十一代孫襲封衍聖公元措修之，官給其費。

translations.literal: The temple at Queli was first restored starting in the ninth year of Taizong (1237), when the fifty-first-generation descendant of the Prior Sage, Yuan Cuo, who held the hereditary title Duke Continuator of the Sage, was ordered to repair it, and the government supplied the expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration of the temple at Queli began in the ninth year of Taizong (1237), when Yuan Cuo—the fifty-first-generation descendant of the Prior Sage and holder of the hereditary title Duke Continuator of the Sage—was ordered to repair it at government expense.

sentences.zh: 而代祠之禮，則始於武宗。

translations.literal: The rite of proxy sacrifice, however, began under Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: The rite of proxy sacrifice, however, began under Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 牲用太牢，禮物別給白金一百五十兩，彩幣表裏各十有三匹。

translations.literal: Victims used the full tai lao sacrifice; gifts were separately supplied of one hundred fifty taels of white silver and thirteen bolts of colored silk each for outer and inner garments.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were offered as a full tai lao sacrifice, with gifts of one hundred fifty taels of white silver and thirteen bolts of colored silk each for outer and inner garments.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，復遣祭酒劉賡往祀，牲禮如舊。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year (1311), the Rector of the Imperial College Liu Geng was again dispatched to perform the sacrifice; the victims and ritual gifts were as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year (1311), Rector of the Imperial College Liu Geng was again dispatched to sacrifice there; victims and ritual gifts were as before.

sentences.zh: 延祐之末，泰定、天歷初載，皆循是典，錦幣雜彩有加焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yanyou era and in the opening years of Taiding and Tianli, all followed this precedent, with brocade silks and assorted colors added.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yanyou and in the opening years of Taiding and Tianli, the court followed this precedent, adding brocade silks and assorted colors.

sentences.zh: 嶽鎮海瀆

translations.literal: Mountains, Peaks, Seas, and Rivers
translations.idiomatic: Mountains, Peaks, Seas, and Rivers

sentences.zh: 嶽鎮海瀆代祀，自中統二年始。

translations.literal: Proxy sacrifice at the mountains, peaks, seas, and rivers began in the second year of Zhongtong (1261).
translations.idiomatic: Proxy sacrifice at the sacred mountains, guardian peaks, seas, and rivers began in the second year of Zhongtong (1261).

sentences.zh: 凡十有九處，分五道。

translations.literal: In all there were nineteen sites, divided into five routes.
translations.idiomatic: There were nineteen sites in all, divided into five routes.

sentences.zh: 後乃以東嶽、東海、東鎮、北鎮為東道，中嶽、淮瀆、濟瀆、北海、南嶽、南海、南鎮為南道，北嶽、西嶽、后土、河瀆、中鎮、西海、西鎮、江瀆為西道。

translations.literal: Later they grouped the Eastern Peak, Eastern Sea, Eastern Guardian Peak, and Northern Guardian Peak as the eastern route; the Central Peak, Huai River, Ji River, Northern Sea, Southern Peak, Southern Sea, and Southern Guardian Peak as the southern route; and the Northern Peak, Western Peak, Queen of Earth, Yellow River, Central Guardian Peak, Western Sea, Western Guardian Peak, and Yangtze River as the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court grouped the Eastern Peak, Eastern Sea, Eastern Guardian Peak, and Northern Guardian Peak as the eastern route; the Central Peak, Huai River, Ji River, Northern Sea, Southern Peak, Southern Sea, and Southern Guardian Peak as the southern route; and the Northern Peak, Western Peak, Queen of Earth, Yellow River, Central Guardian Peak, Western Sea, Western Guardian Peak, and Yangtze River as the western route.

sentences.zh: 既而又以驛騎迂遠，復為五道，道遣使二人，集賢院奏遣漢官，翰林院奏遣蒙古官，出璽書給驛以行。

translations.literal: Since the relay-courier routes proved too long, they restored five routes; each route dispatched two envoys—the Academy of Gathered Worthies memorializing to send Han officials and the Hanlin Academy memorializing to send Mongol officials—and imperial scrolls were issued and relay service granted for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Because relay routes had grown too long, the court restored five routes, each sending two envoys: the Academy of Gathered Worthies recommending Han officials and the Hanlin Academy recommending Mongol officials, with imperial scrolls issued and relay service granted for the journey.

sentences.zh: 中統初，遣道士，或副以漢官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong, Taoist priests were dispatched, sometimes assisted by Han officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongtong, Taoist priests were dispatched, sometimes assisted by Han officials.

sentences.zh: 至元二十八年正月，帝謂中書省臣言曰：「五嶽四瀆祠事，朕宜親往，道遠不可。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan (1291), the emperor said to members of the Secretariat, "For sacrifices at the Five Sacred Mountains and Four Great Rivers, I ought to go in person, but the roads are too far.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan (1291), the emperor told members of the Secretariat, "Sacrifices at the Five Sacred Mountains and Four Great Rivers ought to be performed by me in person, but the distances are too great.

sentences.zh: 大臣如卿等又有國務，宜遣重臣代朕祠之，漢人選名儒及道士習祀事者。」

translations.literal: Great ministers such as you also have state affairs; eminent officials should be dispatched to sacrifice on my behalf—among Han Chinese, select eminent Confucian scholars and Taoist priests versed in sacrificial rites."
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers such as yourselves have state affairs as well; eminent officials should be sent to sacrifice in my stead—among Han subjects, choose eminent Confucian scholars and Taoist priests versed in sacrificial rites."

sentences.zh: 其禮物，則每處歲祀銀香合一重二十五兩，五嶽組金幡二、鈔五百貫，四瀆織金幡二、鈔二百五十貫，四海、五鎮銷金幡二、鈔二百五十貫，至則守臣奉詔使行禮。

translations.literal: As for ritual gifts, at each site the annual sacrifice received one silver incense censer weighing twenty-five taels; the Five Sacred Mountains received two gold-embroidered banners and five hundred strings of paper money; the Four Great Rivers received two woven-gold banners and two hundred fifty strings; the Four Seas and Five Guardian Peaks received two gilt banners and two hundred fifty strings; upon arrival, local officials received the imperial envoy and performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual gifts for the annual sacrifice at each site included one silver incense censer weighing twenty-five taels; the Five Sacred Mountains received two gold-embroidered banners and five hundred strings of paper money; the Four Great Rivers two woven-gold banners and two hundred fifty strings; the Four Seas and Five Guardian Peaks two gilt banners and two hundred fifty strings. Upon arrival, local officials received the imperial envoy and conducted the rite.

sentences.zh: 皇帝登寶位，遣官致祭，降香幡合如前禮，惟各加銀五十兩，五嶽各中統鈔五百貫，四瀆、四海、五鎮各中統鈔二百五十貫。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, officials were dispatched to sacrifice; incense, banners, and censers were sent down as in the preceding rite, except that fifty taels of silver were added at each site—the Five Sacred Mountains each receiving five hundred strings of Zhongtong paper money, and the Four Great Rivers, Four Seas, and Five Guardian Peaks each two hundred fifty strings.
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor ascended the throne, officials were dispatched to sacrifice; incense, banners, and censers were sent down as before, with fifty taels of silver added at each site—the Five Sacred Mountains each receiving five hundred strings of Zhongtong paper money, and the Four Great Rivers, Four Seas, and Five Guardian Peaks each two hundred fifty strings.

sentences.zh: 或他有禱，禮亦如之。

translations.literal: For other prayers as well, the ritual was the same.
translations.idiomatic: For other prayers, the ritual was the same.

sentences.zh: 其封號，至元二十八年春二月，加上東嶽為天齊大生仁聖帝，南嶽司天大化昭聖帝，西嶽金天大利順聖帝，北嶽安天大貞玄聖帝，中嶽中天大寧崇聖帝。

translations.literal: As for their titles, in the second month of spring in the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan (1291), additional honors were conferred: the Eastern Peak became Emperor Benevolent and Sagely of Great Life, Equal to Heaven; the Southern Peak, Emperor Illuminating and Sagely of Great Transformation, Regulator of Heaven; the Western Peak, Emperor Compliant and Sagely of Great Benefit, Golden Heaven; the Northern Peak, Emperor Mysterious and Sagely of Great Constancy, Pacifier of Heaven; and the Central Peak, Emperor Revered and Sagely of Great Tranquility, Central Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan (1291), additional titles were conferred: the Eastern Peak became Emperor Benevolent and Sagely of Great Life, Equal to Heaven; the Southern Peak, Emperor Illuminating and Sagely of Great Transformation, Regulator of Heaven; the Western Peak, Emperor Compliant and Sagely of Great Benefit, Golden Heaven; the Northern Peak, Emperor Mysterious and Sagely of Great Constancy, Pacifier of Heaven; and the Central Peak, Emperor Revered and Sagely of Great Tranquility, Central Heaven.

sentences.zh: 加封江瀆為廣源順濟王，河瀆靈源弘濟王，淮瀆長源溥濟王，濟瀆清源善濟王，東海廣德靈會王，南海廣利靈孚王，西海廣潤靈通王，北海廣澤靈祐王。

translations.literal: Additional honors were conferred: the Yangtze River became King Broad-Source, Compliant and Aiding; the Yellow River, King Spirit-Source, Grand and Aiding; the Huai River, King Long-Source, Universal and Aiding; the Ji River, King Clear-Source, Good and Aiding; the Eastern Sea, King Broad-Virtue, Spirit-Gathering; the Southern Sea, King Broad-Benefit, Spirit-Trustworthy; the Western Sea, King Broad-Moisture, Spirit-Penetrating; and the Northern Sea, King Broad-Marsh, Spirit-Blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze River was titled King Broad-Source, Compliant and Aiding; the Yellow River, King Spirit-Source, Grand and Aiding; the Huai River, King Long-Source, Universal and Aiding; the Ji River, King Clear-Source, Good and Aiding; the Eastern Sea, King Broad-Virtue, Spirit-Gathering; the Southern Sea, King Broad-Benefit, Spirit-Trustworthy; the Western Sea, King Broad-Moisture, Spirit-Penetrating; and the Northern Sea, King Broad-Marsh, Spirit-Blessing.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德二年二月，加封東鎮沂山為元德東安王，南鎮會稽山為昭德順應王，西鎮吳山為成德永靖王，北鎮醫巫閭山為貞德廣寧王，中鎮霍山為崇德應靈王，敕有司歲時與嶽瀆同祀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Dade (1298), under Emperor Chengzong, additional honors were conferred: the Eastern Guardian Peak Mount Yi became King Eastern Peace of Primal Virtue; the Southern Guardian Peak Mount Kuaiji, King Compliant Response of Illuminating Virtue; the Western Guardian Peak Mount Wu, King Ever-Tranquil of Accomplished Virtue; the Northern Guardian Peak Mount Yiwulü, King Broad-Tranquility of Constant Virtue; and the Central Guardian Peak Mount Huo, King Spirit-Response of Revered Virtue; an edict ordered local officials to sacrifice at the same seasons as at the sacred mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Dade (1298), under Emperor Chengzong, the Eastern Guardian Peak Mount Yi was titled King Eastern Peace of Primal Virtue; the Southern Guardian Peak Mount Kuaiji, King Compliant Response of Illuminating Virtue; the Western Guardian Peak Mount Wu, King Ever-Tranquil of Accomplished Virtue; the Northern Guardian Peak Mount Yiwulü, King Broad-Tranquility of Constant Virtue; and the Central Guardian Peak Mount Huo, King Spirit-Response of Revered Virtue. An edict ordered local officials to sacrifice at the same seasons as at the sacred mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 郡縣社稷

translations.literal: Prefectural and County Altars of Soil and Grain
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and County Altars of Soil and Grain

sentences.zh: 至元十年八月甲辰朔，頒諸路立社稷壇壝儀式。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month of the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273), regulations for establishing altars and enclosing ramparts of Soil and Grain in all circuits were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month of the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273), the court promulgated regulations for establishing altars and enclosing ramparts of Soil and Grain in all circuits.

sentences.zh: 十六年春三月，中書省下太常禮官，定郡縣社稷壇壝、祭器制度、祀祭儀式，圖寫成書，名《至元州郡通禮》。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the sixteenth year (1279), the Secretariat sent down ritual officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to fix regulations for prefectural and county altars and enclosing ramparts of Soil and Grain, sacrificial vessels, and sacrificial rites; illustrations were compiled into a book titled General Rites of Prefectures and Commanderies of the Zhiyuan Era.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the sixteenth year (1279), the Secretariat ordered Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials to fix regulations for prefectural and county altars and ramparts of Soil and Grain, sacrificial vessels, and rites; the result, illustrated and bound, was titled General Rites of Prefectures and Commanderies of the Zhiyuan Era.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年冬，復下太常，議置壇於城西南二壇，方廣視太社、太稷，殺其半。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Yuanzhen (1296), orders were again sent to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to discuss establishing two altars southwest of the city; their breadth and length were to match those of the Great Altars of Soil and Grain, reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Yuanzhen (1296), the court again ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to consider establishing two altars southwest of the city, each half the size of the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 壺尊二，籩豆皆八，而無樂。

translations.literal: There were two jar-vessels and eight baskets and dishes each, but no music.
translations.idiomatic: There were two jar-vessels and eight baskets and dishes each, but no music.

sentences.zh: 牲用羊豕，餘皆與太社、太稷同。

translations.literal: Victims were a sheep and a pig; everything else was the same as at the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were a sheep and a pig; everything else matched the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 三獻官以州長貳為之。

translations.literal: The three offering officials were the prefectural chief and his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The three offering officials were the prefect and his deputy.

sentences.zh: 郡縣宣聖廟

translations.literal: Prefectural and County Temples of the Proclaimed Sage
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and County Temples of the Proclaimed Sage

sentences.zh: 中統二年夏六月，詔宣聖廟及所在書院有司，歲時致祭，月朔釋奠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Zhongtong (1261), an edict ordered officials of temples of the Proclaimed Sage and local academies to perform seasonal sacrifices and libation offerings on the first day of each month.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Zhongtong (1261), an edict ordered officials of temples of the Proclaimed Sage and local academies to perform seasonal sacrifices and monthly libation offerings on the first of each month.

sentences.zh: 八月丁酉，命開平守臣釋奠於宣聖廟。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the eighth month, local officials of Kaiping were ordered to perform libation offerings at the Temple of the Proclaimed Sage.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the eighth month, officials of Kaiping were ordered to perform libation offerings at the Temple of the Proclaimed Sage.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，詔曲阜林廟，上都、大都諸路府州縣邑廟學、書院，贍學土地及貢士莊田，以供春秋二丁、朔望祭祀，修完廟宇。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, an edict ordered that the forest temple at Qufu and the temple schools and academies of Shangdu, Dadu, and all circuits, prefectures, counties, and districts be granted land to support students and estates for presenting scholars, to supply the spring and autumn ding-day sacrifices and the new- and full-moon rites, and to repair and complete the temple buildings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzong took the throne, an edict granted the forest temple at Qufu and the temple schools and academies of Shangdu, Dadu, and all circuits, prefectures, counties, and districts land to support students and estates for presenting scholars, to fund the spring and autumn ding-day sacrifices and new- and full-moon rites, and to repair the temples.

sentences.zh: 自是天下郡邑廟學，無不完葺，釋奠悉如舊儀。

translations.literal: From then on, temple schools throughout the empire's prefectures and districts were all fully restored, and libation offerings all followed the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter temple schools throughout the empire were fully restored, and libation offerings followed the old rites.

sentences.zh: 郡縣三皇廟

translations.literal: Prefectural and County Temples of the Three Sovereigns
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and County Temples of the Three Sovereigns

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，初命郡縣通祀三皇，如宣聖釋奠禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen (1295), prefectures and counties were first ordered to sacrifice universally to the Three Sovereigns, following the libation rite of the Proclaimed Sage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen (1295), prefectures and counties were first ordered to sacrifice universally to the Three Sovereigns, following the Proclaimed Sage's libation rite.

sentences.zh: 太皞伏羲氏以勾芒氏之神配，炎帝神農氏以祝融氏之神配，軒轅黃帝氏以風後氏、力牧氏之神配。

translations.literal: Great Bright Fuxi was paired with the spirit of Goumang; Flame Emperor Shennong was paired with the spirit of Zhu Rong; Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan was paired with the spirits of Feng Hou and Li Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Great Bright Fuxi was paired with the spirit of Goumang; Flame Emperor Shennong with the spirit of Zhu Rong; Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan with the spirits of Feng Hou and Li Mu.

sentences.zh: 黃帝臣俞跗以下十人，姓名載於醫書者，從祀兩廡。

translations.literal: Ten men from Yu Fu, a minister of the Yellow Emperor, downward, whose names appear in medical books, were given associated worship in the two wings.
translations.idiomatic: Ten figures from Yu Fu, a minister of the Yellow Emperor, downward—whose names appear in medical texts—received associated worship in the two wings.

sentences.zh: 有司歲春秋二季行事，而以醫師主之。

translations.literal: Local officials performed the rites in spring and autumn each year, with physicians presiding.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials performed the rites each spring and autumn, with physicians presiding.

sentences.zh: 嶽鎮海瀆常祀

translations.literal: Regular Sacrifices at the Mountains, Peaks, Seas, and Rivers
translations.idiomatic: Regular Sacrifices at the Mountains, Peaks, Seas, and Rivers

sentences.zh: 至元三年夏四月，定歲祀嶽鎮海瀆之制。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the third year of Zhiyuan (1266), regulations for the annual sacrifice at the mountains, peaks, seas, and rivers were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the third year of Zhiyuan (1266), the court fixed regulations for the annual sacrifice at the sacred mountains, guardian peaks, seas, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 正月東嶽、鎮、海瀆，土王日祀泰山於泰安州，沂山於益都府界，立春日祀東海於萊州界，大淮於唐州界。

translations.literal: In the first month, for the Eastern Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on the Earth-King day Mount Tai was sacrificed to at Tai'an Prefecture; Mount Yi at the border of Yidu Prefecture; on the Beginning of Spring day the Eastern Sea at the border of Laizhou and the Great Huai at the border of Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, for the Eastern Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on the Earth-King day sacrifices were offered to Mount Tai at Tai'an Prefecture and Mount Yi on the border of Yidu Prefecture; on Beginning of Spring day to the Eastern Sea on the border of Laizhou and the Great Huai on the border of Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月南嶽、鎮、海瀆，立夏日遙祭衡山，土王日遙祭會稽山，皆於河南府界，立夏日遙祭南海、大江於萊州界。

translations.literal: In the third month, for the Southern Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on Beginning of Summer day Mount Heng was sacrificed to by distant rite; on the Earth-King day Mount Kuaiji by distant rite—both on the border of Henan Prefecture; on Beginning of Summer day the Southern Sea and Great River were sacrificed to by distant rite on the border of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, for the Southern Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on Beginning of Summer day Mount Heng was honored by distant sacrifice; on the Earth-King day Mount Kuaiji likewise—all on the border of Henan Prefecture; on Beginning of Summer day the Southern Sea and Great River were honored by distant sacrifice on the border of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 六月中嶽、鎮，土王日祀嵩山於河南府界，霍山於平陽府界。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, for the Central Peak and guardian peak: on the Earth-King day Mount Song was sacrificed to on the border of Henan Prefecture and Mount Huo on the border of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, for the Central Peak and guardian peak: on the Earth-King day sacrifices were offered to Mount Song on the border of Henan Prefecture and Mount Huo on the border of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七月西嶽、鎮、海瀆，土王日祀華山於華州界，吳山於隴縣界，立秋日遙祭西海、大河於河中府界。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, for the Western Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on the Earth-King day Mount Hua was sacrificed to on the border of Hua Prefecture and Mount Wu on the border of Long County; on Beginning of Autumn day the Western Sea and Great River were sacrificed to by distant rite on the border of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, for the Western Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on the Earth-King day sacrifices were offered to Mount Hua on the border of Hua Prefecture and Mount Wu on the border of Long County; on Beginning of Autumn day the Western Sea and Great River were honored by distant sacrifice on the border of Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月北嶽、鎮、海瀆，土王日祀恒山於曲陽縣界，醫巫閭於遼陽廣寧路界，立冬日遙祭北海於登州界，濟瀆於濟源縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, for the Northern Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on the Earth-King day Mount Heng was sacrificed to on the border of Quyang County and Mount Yiwulü on the border of Liaoyang Guangning Circuit; on Beginning of Winter day the Northern Sea was sacrificed to by distant rite on the border of Deng Prefecture and the Ji River at Jiyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, for the Northern Peak, guardian peak, seas, and rivers: on the Earth-King day sacrifices were offered to Mount Heng on the border of Quyang County and Mount Yiwulü on the border of Liaoyang Guangning Circuit; on Beginning of Winter day the Northern Sea was honored by distant sacrifice on the border of Deng Prefecture and the Ji River at Jiyuan County.

sentences.zh: 祀官，以所在守土官為之。

translations.literal: Sacrificing officials were the local territorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing officials were the local territorial officials.

sentences.zh: 既有江南，乃罷遙祭。

translations.literal: Once the south of the Yangtze was obtained, distant sacrifices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Once the south of the Yangtze was secured, distant sacrifices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 風雨雷師

translations.literal: Masters of Wind, Rain, and Thunder
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Wind, Rain, and Thunder

sentences.zh: 風、雨、雷師之祀，自至元七年十二月，大司農請於立春後醜日，祭風師於東北郊；

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Masters of Wind, Rain, and Thunder began in the twelfth month of the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), when the Grand Minister of Agriculture requested that on the chou day after Beginning of Spring, the Master of Wind be sacrificed to in the northeastern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Masters of Wind, Rain, and Thunder began in the twelfth month of the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), when the Grand Minister of Agriculture proposed that on the chou day after Beginning of Spring the Master of Wind be sacrificed to in the northeastern suburb;

sentences.zh: 立夏後申日，祭雷、雨師於西南郊。

translations.literal: on the shen day after Beginning of Summer, the Masters of Thunder and Rain be sacrificed to in the southwestern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: and on the shen day after Beginning of Summer the Masters of Thunder and Rain be sacrificed to in the southwestern suburb.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐五年，乃即二郊定立壇壝之制，其儀註闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou (1318), under Emperor Renzong, regulations for establishing altars and enclosing ramparts at the two suburban sites were finally fixed; the detailed ritual procedures are missing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yanyou (1318), under Emperor Renzong, regulations for establishing altars and enclosing ramparts at the two suburban sites were finally fixed; the detailed ritual procedures are missing.

sentences.zh: 武成王

translations.literal: King Martial Completion
translations.idiomatic: King Martial Completion

sentences.zh: 武成王立廟於樞密院公堂之西，以孫武子、張良、管仲、樂毅、諸葛亮以下十人從祀。

translations.literal: A temple to King Martial Completion was established west of the main hall of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with Sun Wu, Zhang Liang, Guan Zhong, Yue Yi, Zhuge Liang, and ten others below them given associated worship.
translations.idiomatic: A temple to King Martial Completion was established west of the main hall of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with Sun Wu, Zhang Liang, Guan Zhong, Yue Yi, Zhuge Liang, and ten others below them given associated worship.

sentences.zh: 每歲春秋仲月上戊，以羊一、豕一、犧尊、象尊、籩、豆、俎、爵，樞密院遣官，行三獻禮。

translations.literal: Each year on the wu day of the middle month of spring and autumn, with one sheep, one pig, sacrificial jar, elephant vessel, baskets, dishes, offering stand, and goblets, the Bureau of Military Affairs dispatched officials to perform the three-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the wu day of the middle month of spring and autumn, with one sheep, one pig, sacrificial jar, elephant vessel, baskets, dishes, offering stand, and goblets, the Bureau of Military Affairs dispatched officials to perform the three-offering rite.

sentences.zh: 古帝王廟

translations.literal: Temples of Ancient Emperors
translations.idiomatic: Temples of Ancient Emperors

sentences.zh: 堯帝廟在平陽。

translations.literal: The temple of Emperor Yao was at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The temple of Emperor Yao stood at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 舜帝廟，河東、山東濟南歷山、濮州、湖南道州皆有之。

translations.literal: Temples of Emperor Shun existed at Hedong, Mount Li in Jinan, Shandong, Puzhou, and Daozhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Temples of Emperor Shun stood at Hedong, Mount Li in Jinan, Shandong, Puzhou, and Daozhou in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 禹廟在河中龍門。

translations.literal: The temple of Yu was at Longmen in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The temple of Yu stood at Longmen in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 至元元年七月，龍門禹廟成，命侍臣持香致敬，有祝文。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhiyuan (1264), when the Yu temple at Longmen was completed, attendant officials were ordered to present incense in reverence; there was an invocation text.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhiyuan (1264), when the Yu temple at Longmen was completed, attendant officials were ordered to present incense in reverence, with an invocation text.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，立伏羲、女媧、舜、湯等廟於河中解州、洪洞、趙城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year (1275), temples to Fuxi, Nüwa, Shun, Tang, and others were established at Xie Prefecture, Hongdong, and Zhaocheng in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year (1275), temples to Fuxi, Nüwa, Shun, Tang, and others were established at Xie Prefecture, Hongdong, and Zhaocheng in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，修會川縣盤古王祠，祀之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year (1278), the shrine of King Pangu at Huichuan County was repaired and sacrifices were performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year (1278), the shrine of King Pangu at Huichuan County was repaired and sacrifices were performed.

sentences.zh: 二十四年閏二月，敕春秋二仲丙日，祀帝堯廟。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the twenty-fourth year (1287), an edict ordered sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Yao on the bing day of the middle months of spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of the twenty-fourth year (1287), an edict ordered sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Yao on the bing day of the middle months of spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，禮部移太常送博士議，舜、禹之廟合依堯祠故事，每歲春秋仲月上旬卜日，有司蠲潔致祭，官給祭物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe (1328), the Ministry of Rites sent a communication to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for the erudites to discuss; the temples of Shun and Yu should follow the precedent of the Yao shrine—each year on a day divined in the first ten days of the middle month of spring and autumn, local officials would purify themselves and sacrifice, with sacrificial goods supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhihe (1328), the Ministry of Rites referred the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for the erudites to decide: the temples of Shun and Yu should follow the Yao shrine precedent—each year on a day divined within the first ten days of the middle month of spring and autumn, local officials would purify themselves and sacrifice, with sacrificial goods supplied by the government.

sentences.zh: 至順元年三月，從太常奉禮郎薛元德言，彰德路湯陰縣北故羑裏城周文王祠，命有司奉祀如故事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhishun (1330), following the proposal of Xue Yuande, Director of Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the shrine of King Wen of Zhou at the old Youli city north of Tangyin County, Zhangde Circuit, was ordered to receive sacrifices from local officials according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Zhishun (1330), following the proposal of Xue Yuande, Director of Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, local officials were ordered to sacrifice at the shrine of King Wen of Zhou at the old Youli city north of Tangyin County, Zhangde Circuit, according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 周公廟

translations.literal: Temple of the Duke of Zhou
translations.idiomatic: Temple of the Duke of Zhou

sentences.zh: 周公廟在鳳翔府岐山之陽。

translations.literal: The temple of the Duke of Zhou was on the southern slope of Mount Qi in Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The temple of the Duke of Zhou stood on the southern slope of Mount Qi in Fengxiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年六月，以岐陽廟為岐陽書院，設學官，春秋釋奠周文憲王如孔子廟儀。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianli (1329), the Qiyang temple was made the Qiyang Academy, with school officials appointed; in spring and autumn libation offerings were performed to King Wen the Cultured and Exemplary of Zhou following the rite of the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianli (1329), the Qiyang temple became the Qiyang Academy, with school officials appointed; in spring and autumn libation offerings were performed to King Wen the Cultured and Exemplary of Zhou following the Confucian temple rite.

sentences.zh: 凡有司致祭先代聖君名臣，皆有牲無樂。

translations.literal: In general, when local officials sacrificed to sage rulers and eminent ministers of former ages, victims were offered but there was no music.
translations.idiomatic: In general, when local officials sacrificed to sage rulers and eminent ministers of former ages, victims were offered but there was no music.

sentences.zh: 名山大川忠臣義士之祠

translations.literal: Shrines to Famous Mountains, Great Rivers, Loyal Ministers, and Righteous Men
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to Famous Mountains, Great Rivers, Loyal Ministers, and Righteous Men

sentences.zh: 凡名山大川、忠臣義士在祀典者，所在有司主之。

translations.literal: For all famous mountains, great rivers, loyal ministers, and righteous men included in the sacrificial canon, local officials in each place presided.
translations.idiomatic: For all famous mountains, great rivers, loyal ministers, and righteous men included in the sacrificial canon, local officials presided in each place.

sentences.zh: 惟南海女神靈惠夫人，至元中，以護海運有奇應，加封天妃神號，積至十字，廟曰靈慈。

translations.literal: Only the goddess of the Southern Sea, Lady Spirit-Beneficent, in the Zhiyuan era, because of miraculous responses in protecting sea transport, received the added divine title Heavenly Consort, accumulating to ten characters; her temple was called Spirit-Compassionate.
translations.idiomatic: Only the goddess of the Southern Sea, Lady Spirit-Beneficent—in the Zhiyuan era, because of miraculous responses in protecting sea transport—received the added divine title Heavenly Consort, ten characters in all; her temple was called Spirit-Compassionate.

sentences.zh: 直沽、平江、周涇、泉、福、興化等處，皆有廟。

translations.literal: At Zhigu, Pingjiang, Zhoujing, Quan, Fu, Xinghua, and other places, temples all existed.
translations.idiomatic: Temples stood at Zhigu, Pingjiang, Zhoujing, Quan, Fu, Xinghua, and other places.

sentences.zh: 皇慶以來，歲遣使賫香遍祭，金幡一合，銀一鋌，付平江官漕司及本府官，用柔毛酒醴，便服行事。

translations.literal: From the Huangqing era onward, envoys were dispatched each year bearing incense to sacrifice at all temples; one set of gold banners and one ingot of silver were entrusted to the Pingjiang official grain-transport office and the prefectural officials, who performed the rite in ordinary dress with fine-haired victims, wine, and sweet wine.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huangqing era onward, envoys were dispatched each year bearing incense to sacrifice at all temples; one set of gold banners and one ingot of silver were entrusted to the Pingjiang official grain-transport office and prefectural officials, who performed the rite in ordinary dress with fine-haired victims, wine, and sweet wine.

sentences.zh: 祝文云：「維年月日，皇帝特遣某官等，致祭於護國庇民廣濟福惠明著天妃。」

translations.literal: The invocation text read: "On this year, month, and day, the emperor specially dispatched such-and-such officials to sacrifice to the Heavenly Consort, who protects the state and shelters the people, broadly aids and blesses with manifest beneficence."
translations.idiomatic: The invocation read: "On this year, month, and day, the emperor specially dispatched such-and-such officials to sacrifice to the Heavenly Consort, who protects the state and shelters the people, broadly aids and blesses with manifest beneficence."

sentences.zh: 功臣祠

translations.literal: Shrines to Meritorious Officials
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to Meritorious Officials

sentences.zh: 功臣之祠，惟故淮安忠武王立廟於杭，春秋二仲月次戊，祀以少牢，用籩豆簠簋，行酌獻禮。

translations.literal: Among shrines to meritorious officials, only the late Loyal and Martial King of Huai'an had a temple established at Hangzhou; on the wu day following the middle months of spring and autumn, he was sacrificed to with the shao lao offering, using baskets, dishes, grain vessels, and offering stands, and the libation-offering rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Among shrines to meritorious officials, only the late Loyal and Martial King of Huai'an had a temple at Hangzhou; on the wu day following the middle months of spring and autumn he was sacrificed to with the shao lao offering, using baskets, dishes, grain vessels, and offering stands, with the libation-offering rite.

sentences.zh: 若魏國文正公許衡廟在大名，順德忠獻王哈剌哈孫廟在順德、武昌者，皆歲時致祭。

translations.literal: Such temples as that of Duke Wen the Correct of Wei, Xu Heng, at Daming, and those of the Loyal and Offering King of Shunde, Qalaqash, at Shunde and Wuchang, all received seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Such temples as that of Duke Wen the Correct of Wei, Xu Heng, at Daming, and those of the Loyal and Offering King of Shunde, Qalaqash, at Shunde and Wuchang, all received seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王而下，祭器不用籩豆簠簋，儀非酌奠者，有司便服行禮，三上香奠酒而已。

translations.literal: From ancient emperors downward, sacrificial vessels did not include baskets, dishes, grain vessels, and offering stands; where the rite was not libation offering, local officials performed the rite in ordinary dress, thrice offering incense and presenting wine only.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient emperors downward, sacrificial vessels did not include baskets, dishes, grain vessels, and offering stands; where the rite was not libation offering, local officials performed the rite in ordinary dress, thrice offering incense and presenting wine only.

sentences.zh: 大臣家廟

translations.literal: Ancestral Temples of Great Ministers
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral Temples of Great Ministers

sentences.zh: 大臣家廟，惟至治初右丞相拜住得立五廟，同堂異室，而牲器儀式未聞。

translations.literal: Among ancestral temples of great ministers, only at the beginning of Zhizhi (1321) did Right Chancellor Bayiju obtain permission to establish five temples, one hall with separate chambers; but the victims, vessels, and ritual procedures are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Among ancestral temples of great ministers, only at the beginning of Zhizhi (1321) did Right Chancellor Bayiju obtain permission to establish five temples in one hall with separate chambers; but the victims, vessels, and ritual procedures are not recorded.
